posts.title: UK Non-Dom Abolition: Your Paraguay Exit Strategy for 2026
posts.excerpt: The UK abolished its non-dom regime on April 6, 2025. Worldwide income is now taxed on the arising basis with a 10-year IHT tail. Here is why Paraguay is the most compelling alternative for the 16,500 millionaires expected to leave Britain this year.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
The UK non-dom regime is dead. As of April 6, 2025, the remittance basis that allowed non-domiciled residents to avoid UK tax on foreign income and gains is gone. Worldwide income is now taxed on the arising basis from day one.

Henley & Partners projects **16,500 millionaires will leave the UK in 2025** — the highest outflow of any country globally. This is not a trickle. This is a door slamming shut.

## What Actually Changed

| Before April 2025 | After April 2025 |
|---|---|
| Non-doms could claim remittance basis — only UK income taxed | Remittance basis abolished entirely |
| Foreign income and gains exempt if not brought to UK | All worldwide income taxed on arising basis |
| IHT only on UK assets | IHT on worldwide assets after 10 years of residence |
| Simple to leave | New 10-year IHT tail follows you |

The new Foreign Income and Gains (FIG) regime offers a temporary 4-year exemption for new arrivals, but for existing residents there is no transition — the change is immediate and unforgiving.

## Where Do You Go?

The traditional alternatives have their own problems in 2026:

**Gibraltar — Cat 2 Status**
- Maximum tax capped at £42,000/year
- Housing crisis, severely limited availability
- OECD pressure making the regime less attractive
- No path to citizenship

**UAE — Dubai**
- True 0% income tax
- Cost of living 2-3x higher than Paraguay (Dubai 1BR: £1,500-2,500/mo)
- **No path to citizenship** — naturalisation only by sovereign decree after 30+ years
- You are always a temporary resident

**Portugal D7**
- NHR regime ended January 2024
- Foreign income now taxed up to **48%**
- Requires 183 days/year physical presence
- 5 years to citizenship, but at enormous tax cost

**Spain Non-Lucrative Visa**
- 47% income tax rate
- Wealth tax on global assets over €700K
- **Cannot work at all** — even remote work is restricted
- 10 years to citizenship

## Why Paraguay

Paraguay offers something none of the above can match in 2026:

| Factor | Paraguay |
|---|---|
| Foreign income tax | **0%** — permanently, by law, no sunset |
| Local income tax | 10% flat (only on Paraguay-source income) |
| Wealth tax | **None** |
| Inheritance tax | **None** |
| Physical presence | **1 visit every 3 years** |
| Citizenship | **3 years** (fastest in the western hemisphere) |
| Cost of living | £900-1,200/month for a couple |
| CRS reporting | **No** — Paraguay does not participate |
| Work allowed | Yes (with RUC — simple registration) |

## The Numbers

A UK resident with £2M in investment assets earning £80,000/year in passive income:

**Stay in the UK:**
- Income tax on £80K: ~£27,000
- IHT exposure on £2M estate: £800,000 at death
- **Total annual tax: ~£27,000**

**Move to Paraguay:**
- Foreign income tax: **£0**
- Wealth tax: **£0**
- IHT: **£0**
- **Total annual tax: ~£0**

**Annual saving: £27,000. Lifetime IHT saving: £800,000.**

## What About the IHT Tail?

The new rules create a 10-year IHT tail for UK residents who leave. This means your worldwide assets remain within UK IHT for 10 years after departure. It is real. It requires planning.

However:
- After 10 years, you are fully free of UK IHT
- Paraguay has **no inheritance tax** — so in year 11+, your estate faces zero tax in both jurisdictions
- The IHT tail is temporary; Paraguay's 0% is permanent

## Next Steps

The window for proactive planning is now. Every month you wait is another month of tax on worldwide income you could keep.

Agenda a free 30-minute consultation with our team. We will map your specific UK tax situation, explain the SRT (Statutory Residence Test), and show you exactly what Paraguay residency would mean for your numbers.

posts.title: Paraguay vs Portugal for UK Expats in 2026: The Honest Comparison
posts.excerpt: Portugal was the #1 relocation destination for UK expats. Then the NHR regime died. Here is the honest, side-by-side comparison of Paraguay vs Portugal for residency, tax, citizenship, and cost of living in 2026.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
For a decade, Portugal was the default answer for any UK expat looking for a European exit. The Non-Habitual Resident (NHR) regime offered 10 years of 10% tax on foreign pensions and 0% on most foreign income — all while living in the sun with EU passport access.

That era ended in January 2024. And the alternatives in 2026 look very different.

## The Head-to-Head

| Factor | Paraguay | Portugal |
|---|---|---|
| **Foreign income tax** | **0%** — permanent, by law | Up to **48%** progressive (NHR dead) |
| **Local income tax** | 10% flat | 14.5-48% progressive |
| **Wealth tax** | None | None (but AIMI 0.4-0.7% on property >€600K) |
| **Minimum income** | **$0** | €8,460/yr (D7) or €3,280/mo (D8) |
| **Physical presence** | **1 visit every 3 years** | 183 days/year strictly enforced |
| **Citizenship** | **3 years** | 5 years (with A2 Portuguese test) |
| **Passport power** | ~145 countries visa-free | ~189 countries (EU) |
| **Cost of living (couple)** | **£900-1,200/mo** | £2,000-3,000/mo |
| **CRS reporting** | **No** | Yes (full EU transparency) |
| **Work allowed** | Yes (with RUC) | Yes (D8, but restricted D7) |

## What Changed in Portugal

The NHR regime was officially closed to new applicants from January 1, 2024. The replacement, the IFICI regime, only benefits researchers, scientists, and tech professionals. For everyone else:

- Pensions are now taxed at progressive **Portuguese rates up to 48%**
- Foreign dividends and rental income: **28% flat**
- Foreign employment income: **progressive up to 48%**
- No more 10-year holiday

The Portugal dream for tax optimizers is over.

## The Tax Numbers: A Real Example

UK expat with £50,000/year in UK pension income:

**Portugal D7:**
- Pension taxed at progressive rates: ~£12,000/year in tax
- Requires 183 days/year in-country
- Must rent or buy property (Lisbon 1BR: £800+/mo)
- **Net after tax and housing: ~£24,000/year**

**Paraguay:**
- Pension taxed: **£0** (foreign income, territorial system)
- Requires 1 visit every 3 years
- Cost of living for a couple: £900-1,200/mo all-in
- **Net after tax and housing: ~£36,000/year**

**Difference: £12,000 more disposable income per year in Paraguay.**

## The One Real Advantage Portugal Still Has

The EU passport. Portugal gives you citizenship in 5 years and with it, the right to live, work, and retire anywhere in the EU. It is the most powerful passport in the world.

Paraguay's passport gives visa-free access to ~145 countries including the entire Schengen zone (90 days), UK, and most of Latin America — but not the right to live in the EU.

**When Portugal still wins:** You need EU freedom of movement, you have family in Europe, or your income is low enough that the tax difference is small.

**When Paraguay wins:** You care about keeping your money, you do not need to live in Europe full-time, or the tax saving exceeds the value of an EU passport.

## The Hidden Costs of Portugal

| Cost | Portugal | Paraguay |
|---|---|---|
| NHR is dead | Pension taxed up to 48% | 0% on foreign income |
| Mandatory presence | 183 days/year | 1 visit/3 years |
| Property costs (buying) | 6-8% transaction tax | 2-3% total |
| Property costs (renting) | Lisbon 1BR: £800-1,200 | Asunción 1BR: £300-400 |
| Healthcare | Public + mandatory private | Private insurance £40-120/mo |
| Banking | CRS reported to HMRC | No CRS reporting |
| Exit after 5+ years | May face exit tax if Citizenship not secured | Clear exit, no penalties |

## When Paraguay Makes Sense for UK Expats

- Your primary goal is **tax optimization** — keep more of your pension, investment, or business income
- You are **not required to live in Europe full-time** — you want flexibility
- You want **fast citizenship** — Paraguay grants it in 3 years, Portugal in 5-6
- You want **permanent residency from day one** — Portugal starts with temporary renewable visas
- You want **no physical presence requirement** — you travel, you have a second home elsewhere

## When Portugal Still Makes Sense

- EU citizenship is non-negotiable and you are willing to pay the 48% tax to get it
- You need proximity to family in Europe
- You require European healthcare infrastructure
- Your income is modest and the tax difference is small

## The Verdict

In 2026, the question is no longer "Portugal or Paraguay?" for the UK expat. The question is: **"Is an EU passport worth paying 48% tax for the next 5 years?"**

For most UK expats with meaningful savings or pensions, the answer is no. Paraguay saves you tens of thousands of pounds per year, gives you a path to citizenship in less time, and requires almost nothing from you in terms of physical presence.

Come talk to us. We will run your numbers side by side — Portugal vs Paraguay — so you can decide on data, not marketing.

posts.title: DAC8 is Live: Europe's Crypto Reporting Law and Why Paraguay Is the Escape Route
posts.excerpt: DAC8 went live January 2026. All EU crypto exchanges now report holdings and transactions to your local tax authority. For crypto investors in Europe, this changes everything. Here is why Paraguay is the most compelling option for a crypto tax exit.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
January 2026 marked a turning point for crypto investors in Europe. DAC8 — the EU's eighth Directive on Administrative Cooperation — went live, and with it, the era of anonymous crypto holdings in Europe is over.

## What DAC8 Does

From January 1, 2026, all crypto-asset service providers registered in the EU are required to:

- Report every customer's **transactions, holdings, and gains** to their home tax authority
- Automatically exchange this data with all other EU member states
- Report **historical data** going back to January 2023
- Cover all crypto-assets: Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, DeFi tokens, NFTs

The reporting is granular, automated, and mutual. Your crypto portfolio is no longer private from your tax authority.

## What This Means by Country

| Country | Crypto Tax Rate | Current Impact of DAC8 |
|---|---|---|
| Netherlands | **36% on unrealised gains** (Box 3, from 2028) | Massive — being taxed on gains you have not realised |
| Germany | 26.375% on gains <1yr held, **0% after 1yr** | Worst for traders and stakers |
| Spain | 19-28% on gains (sliding scale) | + wealth tax on global assets over €700K |
| France | 30% flat (PFU) | Simple but high — 30% on every trade |
| Italy | **33% from 2026** (up from 26%) | Regulatory tightening + tax increase |
| UK | 10-24% on gains | Non-dom abolition compounds the problem |

**The Netherlands case is the most extreme.** The Box 3 reform (effective 2028) will tax crypto holdings at **36% of deemed or actual returns** — including unrealised gains. If you hold EUR 500K in crypto that appreciates by 20%, you owe EUR 36,000 in tax **even if you did not sell a single coin**.

## How Paraguay Solves This

Paraguay offers a clean escape from the DAC8 reporting web:

| Factor | EU (Your Country) | Paraguay |
|---|---|---|
| Crypto capital gains tax | 19-36% depending on country | **0%** (crypto = goods, territorial system) |
| Wealth tax on crypto holdings | Yes (Netherlands 36%, Spain 0.2-3.5%) | **0%** |
| CRS reporting | Yes — full transparency | **No CRS** |
| DAC8 reporting | Yes — exchanges report automatically | **Not in the EU** — no DAC8 |
| Physical presence required | 183 days/year | **1 visit every 3 years** |
| Citizenship | Your country | **3 years** |

Paraguay classifies crypto as "goods" for natural persons under its tax code. This means:

- Buying and selling crypto is **not a taxable event** (you are trading goods, not securities)
- Capital gains on crypto are **0%** under the territorial system
- There is **no wealth tax** on crypto holdings
- Paraguay does **not participate in CRS** — your crypto stays private
- Paraguay is **not in the EU** — DAC8 does not apply

## But What About DNIT Resolution 47/2026?

In March 2026, Paraguay's tax authority (DNIT) introduced a new resolution requiring certain taxpayers to disclose their crypto holdings.

This is **critical to understand**: Resolution 47/2026 is a **reporting obligation**, not a **tax**. Paraguay is not taxing your crypto. They are simply asking for disclosure to monitor for money laundering and terrorist financing — standard international practice.

Compare this to your EU country: your government taxes your crypto AND receives full DAC8 reports. Paraguay just asks you to file a form, without taxing the gains.

## The Numbers

Italian crypto investor with EUR 200K in crypto, earning 15% annual gains:

**Stay in Italy (2026+):**
- Capital gains tax (33%): EUR 9,900/year
- DAC8 reporting: full transparency to Agenzia delle Entrate
- Wealth tax (IVAFE 0.2%): EUR 400/year
- **Total: EUR 10,300/year in tax**

**Move to Paraguay:**
- Capital gains tax: **EUR 0**
- Wealth tax: **EUR 0**
- Reporting: simple annual form to DNIT — not a tax
- **Total: EUR 0 in tax**

**Annual saving: EUR 10,300. Lifetime: EUR 300,000+ over a 30-year horizon.**

## Crypto-Friendly Banking in Paraguay

| Service | Type | Details |
|---|---|---|
| **X4T** | Licensed crypto exchange | Paraguay-licensed, bank-integrated |
| **Ueno** | Digital bank | Crypto-friendly, English app |
| **Oobit** | Crypto payments | Spend crypto directly |
| **Schwab International** | US brokerage | Accessible from PY |

## Next Steps

If you hold meaningful crypto assets and are a tax resident of an EU country, DAC8 changes your calculus. The window to restructure your residency before your 2026 DAC8 report hits your tax authority's inbox is closing.

We work with crypto investors regularly. Our team understands the specific needs: 0% CGT jurisdiction, no CRS, no wealth tax, and a jurisdiction that treats crypto as property, not a security.

posts.title: FEIE + Paraguay: How Americans Can Earn Up to $132,900 Tax-Free in 2026
posts.excerpt: The Foreign Earned Income Exclusion lets US citizens exclude up to $132,900 of foreign-earned income from US tax. Combined with Paraguay's 0% territorial tax, the result is a near-zero effective tax rate for American expats. Here is how it works.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
Americans living abroad face a unique problem: the US taxes your worldwide income regardless of where you live. It is called citizenship-based taxation, and only two countries in the world do it (the US and Eritrea).

But there is a powerful tool designed exactly for this situation: the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion (FEIE). And when you pair it with Paraguay's territorial tax system, you can earn up to **$132,900 completely tax-free** — no US tax, no Paraguay tax, no tax anywhere.

## How FEIE Works

The FEIE (Section 911 of the Internal Revenue Code) allows US citizens and resident aliens to exclude foreign-earned income from US taxation. For 2026, the exclusion is **$132,900**.

To qualify, you must pass one of two tests:

**Bona Fide Residence Test:** You are a bona fide resident of a foreign country for an uninterrupted period that includes a full tax year.

**Physical Presence Test:** You are physically present in a foreign country for at least 330 days in any 12-month period.

If you qualify, the first $132,900 of your foreign-earned income is exempt from US federal income tax. You still need to file (Form 2555), but you pay zero on that income.

## The Paraguay Advantage

Here is the critical part: FEIE exempts you from **US** tax on foreign income. But you still need to live somewhere that does not tax that income either. Otherwise, you just shift your tax burden from the IRS to a foreign government.

That is where Paraguay comes in.

| Scenario | US Tax | Local Tax | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live in Spain (NLV) | $0 (FEIE) | Up to 47% + wealth tax | **Up to $62,000** |
| Live in Portugal D7 | $0 (FEIE) | Up to 48% (post-NHR) | **Up to $63,000** |
| Live in Costa Rica | $0 (FEIE) | 0% foreign income, 15% local | **$0 (if income is foreign)** |
| Live in Thailand | $0 (FEIE) | Up to 35% if remitted | **Up to $46,500** |
| **Live in Paraguay** | **$0 (FEIE)** | **0% on foreign income** | **$0** |

**Paraguay is the only jurisdiction that completes the full stack: FEIE + 0% local tax + no wealth tax + no CRS + citizenship in 3 years.**

## How It Works Step by Step

1. **Establish foreign tax residence** in Paraguay. This requires physical presence (bona fide residence test) or 330 days (physical presence test). Paraguay's process is straightforward — 60-90 days to temporary residency.

2. **Earn income through a foreign structure** or as an independent contractor. FEIE covers employee compensation and self-employment income earned outside the US.

3. **File Form 2555** with your US tax return. Claim the FEIE on your foreign-earned income up to $132,900.

4. **Pay zero Paraguay tax** on that income. Paraguay's territorial system taxes only Paraguay-source income. Your US-earned or internationally-earned income is 0% taxed in Paraguay.

5. **File FBAR and FATCA** as required. Paraguay does not participate in CRS, but US citizens must still report foreign accounts.

## The Numbers

American freelancer earning $120,000/year working remotely from Asunción:

**Living in the US:**
- Federal income tax: ~$18,000
- Self-employment tax: ~$16,000
- State tax (e.g., California): ~$6,000
- **Total: ~$40,000**

**Living in Paraguay (FEIE + territorial):**
- US federal tax: **$0** (FEIE covers $120K)
- Self-employment tax: **$0** (FEIE applies to SE income with proper structure)
- Paraguay tax: **$0** (foreign income)
- **Total: ~$0**

**Annual saving: $40,000.**

## What About Income Over $132,900?

If you earn more than the FEIE threshold, the excess is still subject to US tax. However:

- The Foreign Tax Credit can offset US tax on excess income if you pay tax to Paraguay — but you won't, because Paraguay taxes local income at 10%
- Consider splitting income: $132,900 through FEIE, remaining through a foreign corporation taxed at Paraguay's 10% corporate rate
- Paraguay's 10% corporate rate is lower than US rates for most earners

## What About FBAR and FATCA?

As a US citizen, you must report foreign bank accounts (FBAR) and specified foreign financial assets (FATCA Form 8938). Paraguay is not a CRS participant, meaning your Paraguay bank accounts are not automatically reported to the IRS.

You still must file these forms voluntarily. But the compliance burden is straightforward — file the forms annually with your tax return.

## What About State Taxes?

If you establish residency in a state with no income tax (Texas, Florida, Nevada, etc.) before moving, state tax is not an issue. If you move directly from California or New York, those states may try to assert continued residency.

**Planning tip:** Establish a domicile in a no-tax state (get a driver's license, register to vote, lease an address) before leaving the US for Paraguay.

## The Bigger Picture

There are 5.5 million Americans living abroad. The number of US citizenship renunciations hit record highs in 2025 (over 6,000 projected). The trend is clear: more Americans are leaving, and those who leave want a jurisdiction that respects the fact that their income is earned outside that country.

Paraguay is the only country that combines:
- **0% foreign income tax** (territorial system)
- **No wealth tax**
- **No inheritance tax**
- **No CRS reporting**
- **Citizenship in 3 years**
- **Cost of living 60-70% lower than the US**

## Next Steps

We help Americans structure their Paraguay residency correctly — including navigating the FEIE qualification requirements, setting up proper business structures, and ensuring FBAR/FATCA compliance.

posts.title: The Truth About Opening a Bank Account in Paraguay
posts.excerpt: Why it's the hardest step and how it's resolved professionally.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Introduction

Every foreigner who arrives in Paraguay with relocation plans hits the same wall: opening a local bank account. It sounds trivial — you walk in, show your passport, walk out with a debit card. In Paraguay, that is not how it works. The banking system is conservative, compliance-driven, and deeply relationship-based. This article explains what actually happens, why it is difficult, and how the process works when done properly.

## Why Is It So Hard?

Paraguayan banks operate under strict anti-money laundering regulations supervised by the SEPRELAD. For a foreigner with no local credit history, no local ID, and no proven income stream in the country, the risk classification is automatically high. Banks respond by demanding layers of documentation that most foreign applicants do not have on hand.

A typical request list includes: certified copy of your passport with entry stamp, proof of residence in your home country, a reference letter from your home bank (often apostilled), proof of income or net worth, your local tax ID (RUC), and a utility bill showing a Paraguayan address. Gathering these from abroad takes weeks.

## Which Banks Work for Foreigners?

Not all banks are equally open to foreign clients. Itaú Paraguay, Banco Continental, and Sudameris have the most experience with international clients, but each has different risk appetites. Some require a minimum deposit of USD 5,000 to USD 25,000. Others will not open an account for a non-resident at all without a local company already registered.

The key variable is whether you already have your temporary residency or at minimum your cedula (local ID) in progress. Without one of these, your options narrow significantly.

## The Role of a Local Introducer

This is the most underestimated factor. A personal introduction from a lawyer, accountant, or existing client who has a relationship with the bank manager changes everything. Paraguay is a relationship-driven economy. Walking in cold as a foreigner gets you the standard compliance treatment — slow, document-heavy, high chance of rejection. Walking in with a professional introducer from a known firm like Nexa Paraguay can reduce the process from weeks to days.

The introducer's firm vouches for the source of funds and the legitimacy of the applicant. This is not an official requirement, but in practice it is often the deciding factor.

## The Application Process Step by Step

The real process looks nothing like opening an account in Europe. First, your team submits a pre-application package to the bank's compliance department for a preliminary review. This includes scanned copies of all documents and a summary of your profile. The bank responds within 3–5 business days with either approval in principle or a list of additional requirements.

Once pre-approved, you attend a face-to-face meeting at the bank branch in Asunción. This is mandatory. The bank officer will ask about your source of income, your intended use of the account, and your plans in Paraguay. This meeting is not a formality — it is a genuine compliance interview.

After the meeting, the final documentation is submitted, and the account is opened within 24–48 hours. You receive your account number and access credentials. Physical debit cards arrive by mail within 10 business days.

## Common Pitfalls

The most frequent mistake is bringing documents that are not apostilled. Paraguayan banks require Hague apostilles on any foreign-issued document used for compliance purposes, including bank reference letters and proof of address. Another common error is not having the documents translated by a Paraguayan sworn translator. Documents in English, German, or Dutch are not accepted.

The third major pitfall is assuming one bank is enough. Many foreigners open accounts at two different banks as a contingency, since bank policies can change without notice.

## How Nexa Paraguay Handles This

We maintain relationships with the compliance departments of four major banks. Before our clients travel to Paraguay, we pre-submit their documentation and secure preliminary approval. We arrange the introducer meeting, accompany the client to the bank, and handle all follow-up. What takes a foreigner weeks of frustration takes, with our support, a single coordinated morning.

## Próximos pasos

If you are evaluating Paraguay seriously, the best way to move forward is a free 30-minute consultation. We do them in Dutch, English, German, or Spanish — no commitment.

posts.title: Australia & New Zealand to Paraguay: The Undiscovered Relocation Route
posts.excerpt: Australia's 47% top marginal tax rate, a housing crisis, and almost zero competition for the Paraguay corridor — this is the route that virtually no one is talking about, and why that creates opportunity for those who act early.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## The Undiscovered Corridor

In 2025, approximately 420,000 Australians left the country permanently or long-term — the largest outflow on record. The top destinations were the UK, New Zealand, the US, and Singapore. Paraguay does not appear anywhere on the radar of most Australian emigration consultants. This is precisely the opportunity.

When a relocation corridor has "almost zero competition," it means:

- Property prices have not been inflated by expat demand
- Professional services are attentive and responsive (you are not just another applicant in a queue)
- The community is small enough to be genuinely welcoming
- Immigration authorities are less likely to tighten requirements due to overwhelming application volumes

## Why Australians and New Zealanders Are Looking Abroad

### Tax Pressure

Australia's tax system is increasingly aggressive for high-income earners. The top marginal rate of 45% kicks in at AUD 190,000, and when you add the 2% Medicare levy, the effective rate reaches 47%. For a professional earning AUD 250,000–500,000, this means approximately AUD 110,000–235,000 goes to the ATO each year.

New Zealand's system is structurally similar: top rate of 39% at NZD 180,000, plus ACC levies. While slightly lower than Australia, the absence of a capital gains tax in NZ is offset by the fact that the bright-line test and other property rules effectively capture gains.

In both countries, the tax burden on investment income is particularly heavy. Dividend income is taxed at marginal rates, capital gains on investments held less than 12 months are taxed as income, and there is no territorial exemption — your worldwide income is subject to tax.

### Housing Crisis

Australian median housing prices reached AUD 1.1 million in Sydney and AUD 780,000 in Melbourne in 2025. In New Zealand, Auckland's median price is NZD 1.05 million. For someone earning an above-average salary, the dream of owning a home in a desirable area is increasingly out of reach.

In Paraguay, the same amount that buys a 2-bedroom apartment in a commuter suburb of Sydney buys:

- A 4-bedroom house with pool in an exclusive neighborhood of Asunción (AUD 250,000–400,000)
- A 3-bedroom penthouse in Villa Morra (the Beverly Hills of Asunción) for AUD 200,000–300,000
- A 10-hectare rural estate within 30 minutes of the city (AUD 300,000–500,000)
- Two separate properties — a city apartment and a countryside weekend home

### Lifestyle Burnout

The "Australian dream" of a 9-to-5 job, mortgage, and two weeks of annual leave is being reassessed by a generation that watched their parents work through recessions, housing booms, and now a cost-of-living crisis. The same dynamics apply in New Zealand. Paraguay offers a genuine alternative: a slower pace of life, lower expenses, and the ability to work remotely while keeping your Australian or New Zealand income.

## Paraguay's Tax System for Australians and New Zealanders

Paraguay's territorial tax system is the central attraction. As a Paraguayan tax resident:

- Your Australian or New Zealand salary is taxed at 0% by Paraguay
- Your investment income (dividends, capital gains, interest from foreign sources) is taxed at 0%
- Your rental income from properties in Australia/NZ is taxed at 0%
- There is no wealth tax, no inheritance tax, and no GST/VAT on foreign transactions

You remain a tax resident of Paraguay as long as you spend more than 120 days per year in the country. Note that both Australia and New Zealand have their own tax residency tests — you must carefully manage your exit to avoid remaining a tax resident of your home country.

### The ATO Exit Process

The Australian Tax Office (ATO) applies a "residence test" that considers:

1. Whether you are physically present in Australia for more than 183 days
2. Whether your permanent place of abode is in Australia
3. Whether your family, economic, and social ties remain in Australia

To successfully cease Australian tax residency, you must demonstrate a clear break. This means severing or substantially reducing each of these ties. Practical steps include:

- Selling or long-term leasing your Australian home
- Closing Australian bank accounts or converting to non-resident accounts
- Informing the ATO of your departure using the ATO's departure notification system
- Moving your superannuation to a self-managed fund with international investment exposure
- Registering with the Australian Electoral Commission as an overseas voter (and demonstrating you are no longer an ordinary resident)

New Zealand follows a similar framework with the "permanent place of abode" test.

## The Residency Process for Australians and New Zealanders

### Document Requirements

The process is simpler for Australian and New Zealand applicants than for South Africans, because both countries are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention and have efficient document issuance systems.

**Required documents:**

1. **Police clearance:** AFP National Police Check (Australia) or Ministry of Justice Criminal Record (New Zealand)
2. **Birth certificate:** Standard birth certificate (full/extract version)
3. **Marriage certificate (if applicable):** Standard version
4. **Passport:** Valid for at least 6 months

**Apostille process:**

- **Australia:** The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) provides apostille services at its Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, and Canberra offices. Turnaround is 2–5 business days. Cost: AUD 82 per document.
- **New Zealand:** The Department of Internal Affairs provides apostille services. Turnaround is 3–5 business days. Cost: NZD 50 per document.

**Translation:** Once apostilled, documents must be translated into Spanish by a sworn translator in Paraguay (or at the Paraguayan consulate in Australia/NZ). Cost: approximately $20–40 per document.

### Application Timeline

| Phase | Duration |
|-------|----------|
| Document collection and apostille | 2–4 weeks |
| Spanish translations | 1 week |
| Application submission in Asunción | 1–2 days |
| Interpol check and processing | 1–2 weeks |
| Provisional residency granted | 4–6 weeks total |
| Permanent residency (after 2 years) | 2 years |
| Citizenship eligibility (after 3 years) | 3 years total |

## Cost of Living Comparison

| Item | Sydney (AUD) | Asunción (AUD) | Savings |
|------|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| Rent (2-bed apartment, good area) | 3,500–5,000 | 800–1,200 | 70–75% |
| Groceries (monthly) | 600–900 | 300–450 | 50% |
| Dining out (per meal) | 30–60 | 8–15 | 70–75% |
| Healthcare (private insurance) | 400–700 | 80–200 | 65–70% |
| Internet (100Mbps+) | 90–120 | 40–60 | 45–50% |
| Coworking membership (monthly) | 300–500 | 100–240 | 50–60% |

## The Community Factor

There are fewer than 500 Australian and New Zealand expats in Paraguay, which means you will be part of a very small, close-knit community. The existing expats tend to be entrepreneurs, remote workers, and retirees who have made a deliberate choice rather than a default one. The community is welcoming, and new arrivals are quickly incorporated into social networks.

For those worried about isolation, the proximity to Buenos Aires (1.5-hour flight) and São Paulo (2-hour flight) means that big-city amenities are never far away. Direct flights from Asunción to Sydney and Auckland are not available, but connections through Santiago (LATAM), São Paulo (several airlines), or Dallas/Fort Worth (American Airlines) are efficient.

## Why Now?

The Australia–Paraguay corridor is undiscovered precisely because it is new. As more Australians and New Zealanders face tax increases, housing inaffordability, and lifestyle pressure, Paraguay will inevitably appear on more radars. The first-mover advantage includes:

- Lower property prices before the expat wave
- Faster immigration processing before backlogs build
- A welcoming community that values newcomers
- More time to learn Spanish and integrate before the expat bubble forms

The optimal time to move is before a trend becomes obvious. In the Paraguay–Australia corridor, that is now.

posts.title: Australia's 47% Top Tax Rate vs Paraguay's 0%: The Numbers
posts.excerpt: Australia's top marginal tax rate hits 47% (including Medicare Levy). Capital gains on crypto: up to 47% with a 50% CGT discount for long-term holders. Corporate rate: 30%. Paraguay: 0% on foreign crypto gains, 10% corporate rate, no wealth tax, no CGT. Concrete comparison for Australian crypto investors.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Australia vs Paraguay: A Tax Story of Two Countries

Australian crypto investors face one of the most aggressive tax regimes in the developed world. Between high marginal rates, CGT on crypto disposals, and the ATO's increasingly sophisticated tracking capabilities, the tax burden on digital asset holders in Australia is severe.

Paraguay offers a radical alternative. Here's the full comparison.

## Australia's Tax System: The Full Breakdown

### Personal Income Tax Rates (2025-26)

| Taxable Income | Tax Rate |
|----------------|----------|
| $0 - $18,200 | 0% |
| $18,201 - $45,000 | 16% |
| $45,001 - $135,000 | 30% |
| $135,001 - $190,000 | 37% |
| $190,001+ | 45% |
| **Plus Medicare Levy** | **2%** |
| **Effective Top Rate** | **47%** |

### Crypto Capital Gains Tax

In Australia, cryptocurrency is treated as a CGT asset by the ATO.

**Key rules:**
- Every crypto disposal triggers a CGT event
- This includes crypto-to-crypto trades (e.g., BTC to ETH)
- Airdrops, hard forks, and staking rewards are treated as income
- NFTs are subject to CGT on disposal

**The 50% CGT Discount:**
If you hold crypto for more than 12 months before disposing, you're eligible for a 50% CGT discount. Your taxable gain is halved.

| Scenario | Gain | After 50% Discount | Tax at 47% |
|----------|------|-------------------|------------|
| Short-term (buy/sell in 6 months) | $500,000 | N/A | $235,000 |
| Long-term (hold 3 years) | $500,000 | $250,000 | $117,500 |

Even with the 50% discount, a long-term holder still pays $117,500 on a $500,000 gain.

### Corporate Tax

- Base rate entity (turnover <$50M): 25%
- All other companies: 30%

### Other Taxes

- **GST:** 10% (standard rate)
- **Stamp duty:** Varies by state (up to 7%)
- **Land tax:** Varies by state
- **No inheritance tax** (federal estate duty abolished)
- **No wealth tax**

## Paraguay's Tax System: The Full Breakdown

### Personal Income Tax

| Income Type | Paraguay Rate |
|-------------|--------------|
| Foreign-source income (including crypto) | 0% |
| Paraguayan-source employment income | 10% |
| Paraguayan-source business income | 10% |

### Crypto Capital Gains

| Scenario | Paraguay Rate |
|----------|-------------|
| Foreign crypto trading (on Binance, Coinbase, etc.) | 0% |
| Foreign crypto staking/yield | 0% |
| Foreign DeFi activities | 0% |
| Foreign NFT sales | 0% |
| Paraguayan crypto trading (X4T, local platforms) | 10% (if PY-sourced) |

### Corporate Tax

- Standard corporate rate: 10%
- Small businesses: 10%

### Other Taxes

- **VAT (IVA):** 10% (standard), 5% (some services)
- **Wealth tax:** 0%
- **Inheritance tax:** 0%
- **Property tax:** 0.5%-1% of assessed value
- **Exit tax:** 0%

## The Numbers: Concrete Comparison

### Scenario 1: High-Income Crypto Trader

**Profile:** $1M AUD in crypto, active trader, $300K annual gains

| Tax Item | Australia | Paraguay |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| Crypto trading gains (short-term) | $300,000 x 47% = **$141,000** | **$0** |
| Employment income (if earning $150K AU) | $48,667 | $0 (foreign-source) |
| Medicare Levy | $3,000 | $0 |
| **Total Tax** | **~$192,667** | **$0** |
| **After-tax income** | **$257,333** | **$450,000** |

### Scenario 2: Long-Term Holder Selling

**Profile:** $2M AUD crypto portfolio, held 3+ years, $800K gain

| Tax Item | Australia | Paraguay |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| Gross gain | $800,000 | $800,000 |
| 50% CGT discount applied | $400,000 | N/A |
| Taxable gain | $400,000 | $0 |
| Tax at 47% | **$188,000** | **$0** |
| **Net proceeds** | **$612,000** | **$800,000** |

### Scenario 3: Crypto Business Owner

**Profile:** Running a crypto-related business, $500K profit

| Tax Item | Australia | Paraguay |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| Corporate tax | $500,000 x 25% (base) = **$125,000** | $500,000 x 10% = **$50,000** |
| Dividend to shareholder | $375,000 | $450,000 |
| Tax on dividend (47% top) | $176,250 | $0 (foreign-source) |
| **Total tax burden** | **~$301,250** | **~$50,000** |
| **Effective rate** | **~60%** | **10%** |

## Beyond Tax: What Else Changes?

### CRS and ATO Visibility

**Australia:** CRS participating country. The ATO receives automatic data from financial institutions in 100+ countries. The ATO also has a dedicated Crypto Task Force targeting non-compliant investors.

**Paraguay:** Not a CRS participant. Your financial data stays in Paraguay. No automatic sharing with the ATO or any other tax authority.

### Cost of Living

| Expense | Sydney | Asuncion |
|---------|--------|----------|
| 2BR apartment (city center) | $3,500-$5,500 AUD/month | $700-$1,300 AUD/month |
| Groceries (monthly) | $800-$1,200 | $400-$700 |
| Dining out (meal for two) | $100-$200 | $30-$60 |
| Internet (100Mbps) | $80-$120/month | $45-$70/month |
| **Total comfortable living** | **$5,000-$7,500/month** | **$1,800-$3,000/month** |

### Citizenship

**Australia:** Citizenship after 4 years of permanent residency. Must pass citizenship test. No dual citizenship restrictions (Australia allows it).

**Paraguay:** Citizenship after 3 years of temporary residency. Basic Spanish required. Dual citizenship allowed. No continuous presence requirement.

### Quality of Life Factors

| Factor | Australia | Paraguay |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| Safety | Very safe | Safe (urban precautions) |
| Healthcare | Medicare (public) | Private insurance ($50-100/mo) |
| Education | Excellent | Good (international schools) |
| Infrastructure | Excellent | Good (improving) |
| English proficiency | Native | Limited (Spanish) |
| Time zone | AEST (UTC+10) | PYT (UTC-4) |
| Visa-free travel | 185+ countries | ~130 countries |

## The Exit Strategy: Moving from Australia to Paraguay

### Step 1: Cease Australian Tax Residency

The ATO has strict rules for ceasing residency:

- Intend to leave permanently
- Establish permanent home in Paraguay
- Spend less than 183 days/year in Australia (preferably 0)
- Terminate Australian Medicare, bank accounts, driver's license
- File final Australian tax return

### Step 2: Obtain Paraguay Residency

- Start document preparation (1 month)
- Submit application (1-2 months processing)
- First trip to Paraguay (1 week)
- Receive cedula (1-2 months)
- **Total: 3-6 months**

### Step 3: Transfer Crypto Holdings

- Sell or transfer crypto to your new Paraguayan accounts
- No Australian CGT on disposal after residency ceases (with proper exit planning)
- No Paraguay CGT on foreign crypto

### Step 4: Settle In

- Open Ueno bank account
- Register with X4T exchange
- Set up Oobit for crypto spending
- File DNIT Res 47 annual report

## The Bottom Line

Australia offers a high quality of life, but its tax system is punishing for crypto investors. The 47% top rate (including Medicare), CGT on every crypto disposal, and aggressive ATO enforcement make serious crypto wealth-building difficult.

Paraguay offers 0% tax on foreign crypto gains, a 10% corporate rate, no CRS, and citizenship in 3 years. For an Australian crypto investor with significant holdings, the math is overwhelming: tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars saved annually, a faster path to a second passport, and a dramatically lower cost of living.

The ATO's crypto surveillance is only getting better. DAC8 and CARF will only increase data sharing. The best time to restructure your tax residency was 2024. The second best time is now.

posts.title: Opening a Paraguayan bank account: what actually happens on the day
posts.excerpt: Paraguayan bank accounts for foreigners are harder to open than they were five years ago — and easier than people think. Here's what the bank appointment actually looks like.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
The Paraguayan bank appointment is the single step in our process that investors worry about most. Forums are full of horror stories — "I spent six weeks being passed between branches" or "The compliance officer rejected me without explanation." Those stories are real, but they're almost entirely the result of walking in cold, without a relationship, without prepared documentation, without a file already reviewed.

Here's what a coordinated bank appointment actually looks like when the paperwork is in order.

## Before the day

By the time you walk into the bank, three things are already true:

1. **The bank has seen your file.** We send it 10 days ahead through a named relationship contact — not a generic teller. That person has already flagged any compliance issues and come back with questions. When you arrive, you're not an unknown.
2. **Your documents are pre-approved in format.** Apostille, translations, income source evidence — the bank's compliance desk has green-lit the file form. You walk in with a sheet that says "everything checked."
3. **The specific KYC profile is agreed.** Paraguay's 2023 AML update (Resolución SEPRELAD 137) tightened source-of-funds documentation. We've supplied and matched the evidence to your declared profile ahead of the meeting.

This pre-work is the reason our bank appointments close in 60–90 minutes on the day. Without it, the same paperwork takes 4–6 weeks of back-and-forth.

## What the 60–90 minutes look like

**Minutes 0–10:** welcome, passport verification, file review with the named officer. You sign the KYC declaration.

**Minutes 10–30:** account opening forms. Pick account type (current + savings, USD + PYG multi-currency is standard). Sign the contracts. Initial deposit confirmation.

**Minutes 30–60:** online banking enrollment. They hand you a physical token (yes, still a physical device at most Paraguayan banks in 2026), walk you through first-login, set your initial PIN. You get card-printing scheduled or pick up a provisional card if available.

**Minutes 60–90:** tax registration bridge. If we're opening on the same day as your Migraciones appointment, the bank needs a RUC (tax ID) to fully activate — we coordinate with SET to get provisional RUC issuance in parallel. Cards, tokens, mobile app setup.

That's the day. You leave with an account number, an activation timeline, and a named contact at the bank.

## What activates on the day vs what takes time

**Same day:**
- Account number issued
- Initial USD deposit credited
- Online banking token enrolled
- Mobile app linked

**3–7 business days after:**
- First wire transfer clears (incoming from your home country)
- International debit card arrives

**2–3 weeks after:**
- Local debit card mailed
- Automatic bill-pay / direct-debit enabled
- Full credit-card issuance (separate application)

The physical card delay is the one thing that catches people. Plan cash or international card access for the first 2 weeks in Paraguay.

## Which bank we route you to

We work with four Paraguayan banks and match you to the one whose profile fits yours:

- **Itaú Paraguay** — best for European passports with clean documentation and deposits USD 50K+. Strong international correspondent network.
- **Banco Familiar** — best for locally-focused business accounts. Fastest account activation. Better for smaller deposits and consumer-banking needs.
- **Banco Continental** — best for agribusiness and land-investment programs. Deep rural-branch footprint.
- **Banco GNB** — best for USD-heavy profiles and investors moving from US dollar jurisdictions.

We never commit you to a bank until we've pre-cleared your file with the relationship manager. If bank A rejects, bank B gets the file the next day.

## The documentation that actually matters

Most rejections we see among direct walk-ins are over source-of-funds. Paraguayan banks in 2026 want:

1. Passport + second government ID from your home country
2. Proof of address (utility bill within 90 days)
3. Apostilled certificate of Paraguayan residency application (we provide — this is why the bank usually happens same-day as Migraciones)
4. Income evidence — for employed: last 3 payslips + employer letter. For business owners: last 2 years of company accounts + tax returns. For investors: broker statements + source of wealth declaration.
5. Bank reference letter from your home-country bank — this is the document that takes longest to obtain in Europe. Start early.

The source-of-wealth narrative matters more than total amount. USD 50K from a documented 5-year consulting career clears faster than USD 500K "from investments" without paper trails.

## What we do when banks say no

It happens. Most common reasons: PEP classification (politically exposed person) via someone in your family tree; unexplained deposits in your home-country account history; residency visa from a jurisdiction on FATF grey list; income source that the bank's AML profile doesn't cover.

When a bank declines, we: get written reasons (sometimes verbally), route the file to a bank whose profile accepts it, package differently if needed, escalate to the bank's relationship director if the decline looks procedural rather than substantive.

In 3 years of running Paraguayan setups, zero of our prepared clients have ended the program without an active bank account. The process takes longer for some profiles — it doesn't fail.

## The practical takeaway

The bank day is the hardest hour in the whole 8–12 week program. It's also the one most tightly controlled by a coordinated team. Walk in with prepared documentation, a named contact expecting you, and a pre-cleared file — and the hard hour becomes a 90-minute formality.

**[Book a free consultation](/s/en/nexa-paraguay/contacto)** to scope your specific banking profile before committing to a program. We'll tell you honestly whether your file is straightforward, complex, or needs pre-work before we engage.

posts.title: Best Tax Residencies for Digital Nomads in 2026
posts.excerpt: The best tax residencies for digital nomads in 2026: Paraguay beats Panama, UAE, Portugal (dead), Spain (24% DNV), Greece, and Croatia on tax rate, permanence, and cost. Complete comparison with hard numbers.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## The Golden Era of Tax-Free Nomading Is Here

If you're a digital nomad in 2026, you have more options than ever for legally reducing your tax burden. But the landscape has shifted dramatically. Portugal's NHR regime is dead. Spain's Digital Nomad Visa traps you at 24%. Greece and Croatia offer temporary fixes, not permanent solutions.

Here's the definitive ranking of the best tax residencies for digital nomads in 2026.

## The Great DNV Trap

Digital Nomad Visas (DNVs) exploded in popularity post-COVID. By 2026, 40+ countries offer them. But there's a catch almost nobody talks about:

**Every single DNV is temporary.** Typically 1-2 years, renewable once, then you're out. You build no path to permanence. No citizenship. No real roots.

Worse, they come with income requirements that lock out lower-earning nomads, and tax rates that range from 15% to 30%+.

## Complete Comparison Table

| Factor | Paraguay | Panama | UAE | Portugal | Spain (DNV) | Greece | Croatia |
|--------|----------|--------|-----|----------|-------------|--------|---------|
| **Foreign Income Tax** | **0%** | 0% | 0% | Up to 48% | 24% (Beckham) | 0% (first 7 yrs) | 0% (first 10 yrs) |
| **Local Income Tax** | 10% (PY-sourced) | Up to 25% | 0% | Up to 48% | 24-47% | 9-44% | Up to 30% |
| **Income Requirement** | **$0** | None (residency) | None | €32,832/yr | €32,000/yr | €3,500/mo | €3,000/mo |
| **Visa Type** | **Permanent Residency** | Permanent Residency | Residence Visa | Standard Residency | Temporary DNV (3 yrs) | Temporary DNV (2 yrs) | Temporary DNV (1 yr) |
| **Path to Citizenship** | **3 years** | 5-8 years | No | 6 years | 10+ years (interrupted) | 7 years | 8 years |
| **Physical Presence** | **0 days/yr** | 1 day/2 yrs | 0 days/yr | 183 days/yr | 183 days/yr | 183 days/yr | 183 days/yr |
| **Cost of Living (single)** | **$700-1,100/mo** | $1,200-1,800/mo | $1,800-3,000/mo | $1,500-2,500/mo | $1,500-2,500/mo | $1,000-1,800/mo | $1,000-1,800/mo |
| **Total Relocation Cost** | **$2,900+** | $5,000-8,000+ | $5,000-10,000+ | $3,000-5,000 | $3,000-5,000 | $2,500-4,000 | $2,500-4,000 |
| **Internet Quality** | 50-300 Mbps | 50-200 Mbps | 500+ Mbps | 100-500 Mbps | 100-500 Mbps | 50-200 Mbps | 50-200 Mbps |
| **CRS Reporting** | No | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **DAC8 Crypto Reporting** | **No** | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## 1. Paraguay — The Undisputed Winner

**Overall Score: 9.5/10**

Paraguay is the best tax residency for digital nomads in 2026, and it's not close. Here's why:

**Tax:** 0% on all foreign-sourced income. That means your remote work income, freelance earnings, crypto gains, and business profits from outside Paraguay are completely tax-free. Capital gains on foreign assets? Also 0%.

**Crypto:** Paraguay treats cryptocurrency as goods, not financial assets. Zero capital gains tax. No CRS reporting. No DAC8 reporting. For the 49 million EU crypto holders facing DAC8 in January 2026, Paraguay is the escape hatch.

**Residency:** Paraguay doesn't have a digital nomad visa — it has something better. You get **permanent residency** from day one, not a temporary DNV. No minimum income requirement. You can qualify on savings alone. One visit every three years maintains it.

**Citizenship:** After just 3 years of permanent residency, you can apply for Paraguayan citizenship. That's the fastest citizenship path in the Americas.

**Cost:** Total relocation cost is $2,900+ all-in (lawyer fees, document legalization, migration fees). Monthly burn rate: $700-1,100 for a single person living well.

**Internet:** 50-300 Mbps in Asunción and major cities. Fiber widely available. Multiple 5G carriers.

## 2. Panama — The Strong Contender

**Overall Score: 7.5/10**

Panama has been a tax haven for decades. Territorial taxation means 0% on foreign income. The Friendly Nations Visa gives permanent residency in about 6-12 months.

**Pros:** No tax on foreign income, strong banking sector, US dollar economy, good infrastructure.

**Cons:** Higher cost of living ($1,200-1,800/mo), citizenship takes 5-8 years, physical presence of 1 day every 2 years, slightly higher relocation costs ($5,000-8,000+).

Panama is Paraguay's closest competitor, but loses on citizenship speed, cost, and the fact that Panama's residency requires either a job offer, investment, or professional license — not as straightforward for digital nomads.

## 3. UAE — Zero Tax, Zero Path

**Overall Score: 6.5/10**

The UAE offers a genuine 0% tax environment with no income tax, no capital gains tax, no VAT on most goods.

**Pros:** World-class infrastructure, Dubai lifestyle, 0% tax on everything.

**Cons:** Citizenship is virtually impossible (no path for foreigners). Cost of living is high ($1,800-3,000/mo). The "residency" is a renewable visa tied to employment, freelancing, or property — not permanent. No CRS reporting but increasing pressure for transparency.

The UAE is great for high earners who don't care about citizenship. For digital nomads on a budget or those wanting permanent roots, it falls short.

## 4. Portugal — Dead in the Water

**Overall Score: 3/10**

Portugal was the gold standard for digital nomads and retirees for over a decade. The NHR (Non-Habitual Resident) regime offered 0% on foreign income for 10 years.

**It's over.** NHR was abolished on January 1, 2025. New residents now pay Portugal's progressive rate of up to 48% on worldwide income.

**DNV:** Portugal still has a Digital Nomad Visa, but it comes with a €32,832/year income requirement and subjects you to Portuguese tax rates after the first year. Not competitive.

## 5. Spain — 24% (If You're Lucky)

**Overall Score: 4.5/10**

Spain's Digital Nomad Visa is one of the most popular, but the numbers don't work.

**Income Requirement:** €32,000/year minimum. That's steep for many nomads.

**Tax:** Under the Beckham Law (modified for DNVs), you pay a flat 24% on Spanish-sourced income for the first 4 years. That's better than the standard 47% rate, but it's still 24% on income you could pay 0% on elsewhere.

**Duration:** The visa is valid for 1 year, renewable for up to 5 years. After that, you must switch to standard residency — and standard tax rates.

**No Citizenship Path:** Spain requires 10 years of residency for citizenship (with some exceptions for Ibero-American countries). Your DNV years may not count.

## 6. Greece — Good for a While

**Overall Score: 5.5/10**

Greece offers a 50% tax exemption on foreign income for 7 years for new residents who move their tax residence to Greece.

**Pros:** Great lifestyle, 7-year tax holiday, relatively low cost of living.

**Cons:** The 50% exemption still means you pay Greek taxes on half your income. Physical presence of 183 days/year required. Digital Nomad Visa is temporary (2 years, renewable). Citizenship takes 7 years of continuous residence. CRS and DAC8 reporting apply.

## 7. Croatia — The 10-Year Holiday

**Overall Score: 5/10**

Croatia offers digital nomads 0% tax on foreign income for up to 10 years.

**Pros:** Adriatic lifestyle, 0% foreign income, 10-year window.

**Cons:** The DNV is strictly temporary — 1 year, renewable once. You cannot convert to permanent residency or citizenship through this visa. You must physically reside in Croatia. CRS and DAC8 apply. After 10 years... what then?

## Why Paraguay Beats Them All

Let's be specific about why Paraguay takes the #1 spot:

### Tax: 0% Forever, Not 0% for a While

Greece gives you 7 years. Croatia gives you 10. Portugal used to give you 10. Paraguay gives you 0% **forever** — with no sunset clause, no expiration, no ticking clock. You become a tax resident and your foreign income is permanently exempt.

### Residency: Permanent From Day One

Every DNV on this list is temporary. You're always on probation. Paraguay gives you permanent residency from the moment your application is approved. You're done. No renewals. No uncertainty.

### Citizenship: 3 Years

This is the killer feature. No other country on this list offers citizenship in 3 years. Not even close. Panama is 5-8 years. Portugal is 6. Greece is 7. Spain is 10. UAE: no path at all.

### No Physical Presence

Panama requires 1 day every 2 years. Spain requires 183 days/year. Greece requires 183 days/year. Paraguay requires **zero days per year**. One visit every 3 years to renew your cédula. You can literally live anywhere else and maintain your Paraguayan residency.

### Crypto-Friendly

With DAC8 coming into effect across the EU in January 2026, 49 million European crypto holders need to make a decision. Paraguay doesn't participate in CRS or DAC8. Crypto is treated as goods, not financial assets. Zero capital gains tax. No reporting to your home country.

### The Cost Factor

At $2,900+ all-in for the full residency package and $700-1,100/mo cost of living, Paraguay is both the cheapest to set up AND the cheapest to maintain. No other option comes close on total cost.

## The Bottom Line

| Priority | Best Option |
|----------|-------------|
| Lowest tax overall | Paraguay (0% forever) |
| Fastest citizenship | Paraguay (3 years) |
| Lowest cost | Paraguay ($2,900 setup, $700/mo) |
| Best crypto treatment | Paraguay (0% CGT, no CRS, no DAC8) |
| Least physical presence | Paraguay (0 days/yr) |
| Best infrastructure | UAE (but no path to permanence) |
| Best lifestyle | Subjective (Greece, Spain) |

**If you want a permanent, affordable, tax-free home with a path to citizenship, Paraguay is the only real answer in 2026.**

posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Introduction

The single biggest bottleneck in any Paraguay relocation is document preparation. You cannot expedite this step once you are in the country. Every missing apostille, every untranslated certificate, every document that needs re-issuing from your home country costs you weeks. This checklist is designed to be printed and checked off before you book your flight.

## Documents That Must Be Apostilled in Your Home Country

These documents require a Hague Apostille from the country where they were issued. This must be done before you leave. Paraguayan authorities will not accept documents without it.

| Document | Apostille Required | Sworn Translation Needed | Notes |
|----------|-------------------|-------------------------|-------|
| Birth certificate | Yes | Yes | Must be an official certified copy |
| Marriage certificate (if applicable) | Yes | Yes | Both civil and religious if applicable |
| Criminal record / police clearance | Yes | Yes | Must be issued within 90 days of travel |
| University degrees and transcripts | Yes | Yes | Needed if applying for professional visas |
| Bank reference letters | Yes | Yes | From your home bank, dated within 30 days |
| Proof of income or net worth | Yes | Yes | Tax returns, investment statements, or pension docs |

## Documents to Obtain in Paraguay

Once you arrive, you will need to obtain several local documents. These cannot be prepared in advance.

- **Certificado de Antecedentes Policiales** (local police clearance) — obtained at the Policía Nacional in Asunción. Takes one business day.
- **Certificado de Antecedentes Judiciales** (judicial records) — obtained at the Corte Suprema de Justicia. Same-day service available.
- **Cédula de Identidad Civil** — the Paraguayan national ID card. Requires prior registration with Migraciones.
- **RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes)** — the tax ID number, processed through the SET (tax authority).
- **Proof of address** — a utility bill or rental contract in your name at a Paraguayan address.

## Translations: What You Need to Know

Every foreign-language document submitted to a Paraguayan government office must be translated by a Paraguayan sworn translator (traductor público). Translations done abroad or by non-certified translators are not accepted.

The sworn translator affixes their official seal and registers the translation with the Corte Suprema de Justicia. This adds 2–3 business days per document. Plan for it.

We recommend having all translations done in parallel while your apostilles are being processed. A well-coordinated timeline has translations arriving within the same week as your apostilled originals.

## Originals vs. Copies

Paraguayan bureaucrats want to see original apostilled documents. Photocopies — even notarized ones — are generally not accepted for first-time filings. Bring the originals in a dedicated folder. Keep photocopies as a backup for your own records.

After documents are registered with the relevant authority (Migraciones, SET, Registro Civil), you can request certified copies that subsequent agencies will accept. But the first submission must be originals.

## Digital Documents and QR Codes

As of 2026, some Paraguayan agencies accept apostilles with QR codes that can be verified online. This is true for digital apostilles issued by countries such as the Netherlands, Germany, and the UK. However, the acceptance is inconsistent across agencies. When in doubt, bring a physical apostille. Having both a digital and physical version is the safest approach.

## The Complete Timeline

Assuming you have all documents ready before travel, the document validation phase takes approximately:

- **Week 1:** Sworn translations (3–5 documents, 2–3 days)
- **Week 2:** Police clearance + judicial records in Paraguay (1–2 days)
- **Week 3–4:** Submission to Migraciones for residency (1 day, then wait)
- **Week 5–8:** Government processing of residency (45–60 days)
- **Week 9+:** Cedula issuance, RUC registration, bank account opening

## Common Mistakes

- Apostilling documents that have already expired (police clearances, bank letters have validity windows)
- Not ordering enough certified copies of key documents (birth certificate, marriage certificate)
- Assuming English-language documents will be accepted without translation (they will not)
- Waiting until arrival to start the document process — this adds 4–6 weeks minimum

## How Nexa Paraguay Helps

We review your document package before you travel. Our legal team identifies gaps, advises on apostille requirements specific to your home country, and coordinates with our sworn translators so translations are ready the day your documents arrive in Paraguay. We also maintain a document checklist template customized to your nationality and visa type.

## Próximos pasos

If you are evaluating Paraguay seriously, the best way to move forward is a free 30-minute consultation. We do them in Dutch, English, German, or Spanish — no commitment.

posts.title: Setting Up a Company in Paraguay: Business Types and Steps
posts.excerpt: EAS vs. SA. When to use which, and what each structure actually requires.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Introduction

Paraguay offers two main corporate structures for foreign investors: the EAS (Empresa por Acciones Simplificada) and the SA (Sociedad Anónima). Choosing between them is one of the first and most consequential decisions you will make. This article breaks down the differences in plain language, with real requirements and timelines.

## EAS — Simplified Stock Company

The EAS was introduced in 2019 as a modern, lightweight corporate structure designed for small to medium enterprises and foreign investors. It requires a minimum of one shareholder (individual or legal entity) and one director. There is no minimum capital requirement in theory, but in practice, a capital of USD 5,000–10,000 is recommended for credibility with banks and suppliers.

**Key advantages:**
- Incorporation in 7–10 business days
- No board of directors required
- Shareholder meetings can be held virtually
- No statutory auditor required unless revenue exceeds thresholds
- Can be fully owned by a foreign entity or individual

The EAS is ideal for freelancers, remote workers establishing tax residency, small import-export operations, and holding companies for personal assets.

**Disadvantages:**
- Cannot publicly trade shares
- Less formal structure may be viewed as less credible by some institutions
- Limited to a maximum of 50 shareholders

## SA — Corporation (Sociedad Anónima)

The SA is the traditional corporate structure, more suitable for larger operations. It requires a minimum of two shareholders and a board of directors. The minimum capital is approximately USD 1,000, but for operational credibility, USD 20,000–50,000 is typical.

**Key characteristics:**
- Incorporation in 15–25 business days
- Requires a board of directors with at least two members
- Must appoint a statutory auditor (síndico)
- Shares can be transferred more easily
- More formal governance requirements
- Better suited for joint ventures, large real estate projects, and regulated industries

The SA is the preferred structure for companies seeking bank financing, participating in public tenders, or operating in regulated sectors such as insurance, finance, or telecommunications.

## Comparative Table

| Feature | EAS | SA |
|---------|-----|----|
| Minimum shareholders | 1 | 2 |
| Minimum capital | None (recommended USD 5K+) | ~USD 1,000 (recommended USD 20K+) |
| Incorporation time | 7–10 days | 15–25 days |
| Board required | No | Yes (minimum 2 members) |
| Statutory auditor | No (below thresholds) | Yes |
| Virtual meetings | Yes | Yes |
| Public share offering | No | Yes |
| Best for | SMEs, holding, freelancers | Large ops, regulated industries |

## The Incorporation Process

Regardless of structure, the process follows the same sequence:

1. **Name reservation.** You propose three corporate names to the Registro Público de Comercio. They check availability and reserve your chosen name for 30 days.
2. **Drafting the bylaws.** A Paraguayan lawyer drafts the estatuto social — the company's charter. This must include capital structure, shareholder details, management, and purpose.
3. **Notarization.** The bylaws are signed before a Paraguayan notary public. This requires the physical presence of all shareholders or their legal representatives with power of attorney.
4. **Registration with the Registro Público.** The notarized bylaws are submitted to the commercial registry. This step takes 5–15 days depending on workload.
5. **RUC registration.** Once the company is registered, you obtain the RUC (tax ID) from the SET. This takes 1–2 business days.
6. **Bank account.** With the RUC and registered bylaws, you open a corporate bank account.

## Timeline Reality Check

The 7–10 day EAS timeline assumes all documents are ready: apostilled and translated powers of attorney for foreign shareholders, clear corporate purpose, and no complications with name conflicts or registry backlogs. When documents are incomplete, the timeline can double.

Our experience: a well-prepared EAS incorporation with Nexa Paraguay averages 8 business days from document submission to RUC issuance. An SA averages 18 business days.

## Tax Implications by Structure

Both structures are subject to the same tax regime in Paraguay: 10% IRE (corporate income tax) on locally sourced income, 10% VAT (IVA) on taxable transactions, and withholding taxes on dividend distributions. The structure does not change your tax rate — it changes your compliance obligations. An SA requires more formal accounting, audited financial statements, and board meeting minutes.

## How Nexa Paraguay Handles Incorporation

Our legal team drafts the bylaws, coordinates with the notary, handles the registry submission, and registers your RUC. For foreign shareholders, we prepare and manage the power of attorney process so you can incorporate without traveling. For clients who want to travel, we coordinate the in-person notary signing during your operational day in Asunción.

posts.title: Cost of Living in Paraguay: A Realistic Guide for Europeans
posts.excerpt: Concrete numbers: housing, healthcare, education, services — from a European perspective.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Introduction

One of the main reasons Europeans relocate to Paraguay is the cost of living. But "cheaper than Europe" is not a number. This article provides specific, real-world monthly costs based on actual client data from 2025–2026. All figures are in USD unless otherwise stated.

## Housing: Rent by Neighborhood

Asunción's rental market varies dramatically by neighborhood. The most sought-after areas for expats are Villa Morra, Carmelitas, and San Roque — all in the central-southwest corridor of the city.

| Neighborhood | 2-bedroom apartment (USD/month) | 3-bedroom house (USD/month) |
|-------------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|
| Villa Morra | $600–$900 | $1,000–$1,800 |
| Carmelitas | $500–$800 | $900–$1,500 |
| San Roque | $400–$700 | $700–$1,200 |
| Las Lomas | $700–$1,200 | $1,200–$2,500 |
| Manors (villa-style) | N/A | $1,500–$3,000 |

To put this in perspective: a 2-bedroom in Villa Morra costs about what a studio costs in central Amsterdam or Berlin. A 3-bedroom house with a garden in Las Lomas costs less than a one-bedroom apartment in central London.

Most rental contracts require a deposit of 1–2 months rent and are denominated in USD, though payment is sometimes accepted in guaraníes at the exchange rate of the day.

## Utilities and Services

Electricity, water, gas, and internet for a 2-bedroom apartment in Asunción averages $120–$180 per month. Internet (fiber optic, 300 Mbps) is approximately $45–$60 per month from providers like Personal or Tigo. Electricity is notably cheap due to Paraguay's hydroelectric dominance (Itaipú dam) — you can run air conditioning 24/7 in summer for approximately $80–$120/month.

Mobile phone plans with 20–40 GB of data cost $15–$30 per month. A cleaning service (once per week, 4 hours) costs $60–$100 per month.

## Healthcare

Private health insurance for a healthy individual aged 35–45 costs $60–$120 per month from major providers like BNF or Grupo Médico. Family plans (couple + two children) range from $150–$300 per month. Coverage includes private hospital access in Asunción, outpatient care, and emergency evacuation within the country.

Out-of-pocket costs are also low: a specialist consultation costs $30–$60, dental cleaning is $25–$50, and a full blood panel is $40–$80.

International health insurance with worldwide coverage (excluding the US) runs $150–$300/month for an individual. Most European expats opt for a combination of local private insurance for routine care and international insurance for major events.

## International Education

This is the largest recurring cost for families. International schools in Asunción:

- **American School of Asunción:** $8,000–$12,000 per year
- **Colegio Internacional:** $6,000–$9,000 per year
- **Goethe Schule (German school):** $5,000–$8,000 per year
- **Lycée Français:** $6,000–$10,000 per year

Compared to European international school fees (often $20,000–$35,000 per year in major capitals), the cost is roughly half to a third.

## Groceries and Dining

A monthly grocery budget for a couple eating a mix of local and imported products is $300–$500. Local produce — meat, vegetables, fruits, dairy — is very affordable. Imported products (European cheese, wine, olive oil) carry a premium of 30–80% over European prices.

Restaurant prices: a meal for two at a mid-range Asunción restaurant costs $25–$50. A high-end dinner at a place like Tierra Corazón or La Cabrera is $60–$100 for two with wine. Lunch menus (menú ejecutivo) are $5–$10 per person.

## Total Monthly Budget

A realistic monthly budget for a European couple living comfortably in Asunción:

| Category | Budget (USD/month) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Rent (2-bed, Villa Morra) | $700 |
| Utilities + internet | $150 |
| Private health insurance (couple) | $200 |
| Groceries | $400 |
| Dining out (4x/month) | $150 |
| Cleaning service | $80 |
| Transport (rideshare, occasional taxi) | $100 |
| Miscellaneous | $200 |
| **Total** | **$1,980** |

Compare this to $4,500–$6,000 for a comparable lifestyle in Amsterdam, Berlin, or Paris. The savings are not marginal — they are structural.

## What Costs the Same

Not everything is cheaper. Electronics (laptops, phones), new cars, and flights to Europe cost roughly the same or slightly more. Amazon delivery requires freight forwarders. Import duties on personal shipments can be unpredictable.

## How Nexa Paraguay Helps

Before you commit, we provide a personalized cost projection based on your specific lifestyle, family size, and preferred neighborhood. Our local team also helps with rental contracts, utility setup, and school enrollment — so your first month in Paraguay is about settling in, not bureaucracy.
