posts.title: Paraguay's Real Estate Market: Current Overview
posts.excerpt: Prices by neighborhood in Asunción, yields and risks — without bullish rhetoric.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Introduction

Paraguay's real estate market has attracted significant foreign capital over the past five years. But not all areas are appreciating equally, and not every purchase is a good investment. This article provides a data-driven overview of Asunción's residential market in 2026 — prices, yields, and risks — without the promotional tone common in relocation content.

## Asunción Neighborhoods: Price per Square Meter

Residential property prices in Asunción vary by a factor of three depending on the neighborhood. The following figures are approximate ranges for apartments in good condition (not luxury, not distressed):

| Neighborhood | USD/m² (apartment) | Trend | Profile |
|-------------|-------------------|-------|---------|
| Villa Morra | $1,200–$1,800 | Stable | Most popular with expats. Good infrastructure, restaurants, services. |
| Carmelitas | $1,000–$1,500 | Slight increase | Quieter than Villa Morra. Family-friendly, walking distance to shopping. |
| San Roque | $800–$1,200 | Stable | Up-and-coming. More local character, lower prices, good value. |
| Las Lomas | $1,500–$2,500 | Moderate increase | Premium area. Large houses on large plots. Expensive but still cheap by global standards. |
| Microcentro | $600–$1,000 | Stable | Downtown. Older buildings, more traffic. Lower entry price. |
| Santa Teresa | $700–$1,100 | Stable | Residential, good access to main avenues. |

To provide context: $1,500/m² in Las Lomas buys you a 200m² house for $300,000. In a European capital, $300,000 might buy you a studio apartment.

## Rental Yields

Gross rental yields in Asunción range from 5% to 8% for residential properties, depending on location and property type. This compares favorably to European capitals (2–4%) but is below what some LATAM markets offer.

| Property Type | Gross Yield | Occupancy | Tenant Profile |
|--------------|------------|-----------|----------------|
| 2-bed apartment, Villa Morra | 5–6% | High | Young professionals, expats |
| 3-bed house, Las Lomas | 4–5% | Moderate | Families, diplomats |
| 1-bed apartment, Microcentro | 6–8% | Moderate | Local workers, students |

Yields are gross — before property taxes, maintenance, management fees, and vacancy periods. Net yields typically run 3–5% after all costs. Property tax (Impuesto Inmobiliario) is negligible: approximately $200–$500 per year for a mid-range property.

## Foreign Buyer Trends

The profile of foreign buyers in Paraguay has shifted. Five years ago, the typical buyer was a retiree looking for a low-cost place to live. Today, the typical buyer is a working professional aged 30–50, often with a remote income, buying a primary residence while establishing tax residency.

The most active nationalities are Dutch, German, Swiss, and Argentine. Brazilians remain the largest foreign property owners in Paraguay, but their focus is typically on the border region rather than Asunción.

Most foreign buyers pay in cash or with financing from their home country. Local mortgage financing is available but expensive (12–18% interest rates) and typically requires a 50% down payment. Foreign buyers without local credit history generally cannot access local mortgages.

## Due Diligence Risks

Paraguay's property registry is reliable but not foolproof. The following risks require professional attention:

- **Title encumbrances.** Properties can have undisclosed liens, easements, or ownership disputes. A title search at the Registro de la Propiedad is essential.
- **Succession issues.** Properties inherited without formal division can have multiple heirs, some of whom may not have a clear title.
- **Zoning and planning.** Not all properties have clear zoning documentation. Building permits for renovations may not exist for existing structures.
- **Informal constructions.** Properties expanded without municipal permits are common. These cannot be legally sold as-is.

Every property purchase should include a legal due diligence process conducted by a Paraguayan lawyer with real estate experience.

## The Purchase Process

Buying property as a foreigner is straightforward in Paraguay — there are no restrictions on foreign ownership except for land within 50 km of international borders, which requires a special permit.

The process typically takes 30–60 days: (1) offer and negotiation, (2) due diligence, (3) purchase agreement signed before a notary, (4) payment (usually via escrow or bank transfer), (5) deed registration at the Registro de la Propiedad.

Closing costs are approximately 5–8% of the purchase price, including notary fees, transfer tax, registry fees, and legal fees.

## Market Outlook

Asunción's residential market is stable rather than booming. Prices have appreciated 15–25% in the best areas over the past three years, driven by foreign demand and limited supply of quality housing. New construction is concentrated in Villa Morra, Las Lomas, and the emerging Nu Guasu area.

The market is unlikely to replicate the dramatic appreciation seen in Medellín or Lisbon. Paraguay's economy grows steadily but not spectacularly. For a foreign buyer, the value is in the lifestyle and tax benefits, not in speculative appreciation.

## How Nexa Paraguay Helps

Our property team conducts title due diligence, reviews purchase agreements, coordinates with notaries, and registers the deed. For clients purchasing remotely, we manage the entire process via power of attorney. We also provide property management referrals for rental properties.

posts.title: Week-by-week: what the 8–12 week Nexa process actually looks like
posts.excerpt: We say 8–12 weeks. Here's what happens in each of those weeks — what we do, what you do, and what can slip the timeline.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
Most relocation agencies pitch "one coordinated process" and leave the timeline as a vague promise. We publish our week-by-week because when you're about to move countries, you want to know exactly what's happening on week five.

Here's what the Nexa Business program — residency + company + bank account — actually looks like, week by week.

## The one-line summary

**Week 1:** Consultation and diagnostic. **Weeks 2–5:** Document preparation. **Week 6:** Your trip — one coordinated operational day in Asunción. **Weeks 7–9:** Company incorporation and bank opening. **Weeks 10–12:** Residency approval, cédula issuance, delivery.

Total: 8–12 weeks realistic. 8 is fast-track. 12 is standard when government issuance takes the upper end.

## Week 1 — Initial consultation + diagnostic

**What we do:**
- 30-minute free intro call
- Diagnose fit (is Paraguay actually right for you, or is Uruguay/Panama a better call?)
- Pick the program: Base, Business, Investor, Land
- If you proceed: send the engagement letter and the document checklist

**What you do:**
- One call. Maybe one follow-up email.
- Sign the engagement if you proceed.
- Pay the initial invoice (we don't start without it — this keeps us honest about who we take on).

**What can slip:** nothing material. This is a decision week.

## Weeks 2–3 — Document preparation (your side)

**What we do:**
- Send you a jurisdiction-specific document checklist (Netherlands ≠ Germany ≠ Belgium ≠ Spain — the apostille chains are different)
- Schedule a 45-min prep call to walk through the checklist in detail
- Stay on call for questions

**What you do:**
- Collect: passport, birth certificate, police clearance, marriage certificate (if applicable), bank reference letter
- Get them apostilled in your home country (this is the step that slips timelines most often — budget 10 business days)
- Ship us scans as each one comes in

**What can slip:** your home country's apostille process. The Netherlands is ~5 business days. Germany varies by Bundesland. Italy can take 4 weeks in some regions. If your birth certificate has to be re-issued first (common for people born abroad), add another 2 weeks.

## Weeks 4–5 — Document validation (our side)

**What we do:**
- Paraguayan lawyer reviews every document. Validates format, translations, and sufficiency.
- If anything is wrong, we tell you **now** — not when you're sitting in the Migraciones office.
- We prepare the migration file in parallel: all the Paraguayan-side forms, cover letters, and applications.
- We book your appointments at Migraciones, Identificaciones, and the bank. All on one day.

**What you do:**
- Mostly wait. Answer the occasional follow-up email.
- Book your flight once we confirm the operational day.

**What can slip:** if a document is rejected for form, we loop back to step 2–3 and re-issue. This is why we validate before you travel — a rejection here is a 2-week delay, a rejection after you've flown is a re-flight.

## Week 6 — The operational day

This is the trip. One day in Asunción. Everything scheduled back-to-back.

**Typical day (real client schedule, anonymized):**
- 07:30: Pickup from your hotel, breakfast briefing
- 08:30: Migraciones — residency application filed, biometrics taken
- 10:30: Identificaciones — cédula application, photo, fingerprinting
- 12:30: Lunch at a restaurant in Villa Morra (you've been awake since 6, this is non-negotiable)
- 14:00: Bank appointment — account opening, initial deposit
- 15:30: Notary — company incorporation documents signed (if on Business program)
- 17:00: Wrap-up. You're free. Your Paraguayan paperwork is in motion.

**What you do:** show up. Bring your passport and a few specific documents we'll have listed. Wear something you'd wear to a European bank meeting.

**What can slip:** almost nothing — this is the most tightly coordinated day of the program. The rare slip is the bank introducing a new compliance step mid-meeting; we have a one-day buffer built in.

## Weeks 7–9 — Company incorporation + bank activation

**What we do:**
- File company incorporation with the Paraguayan registry
- Obtain the RUC (tax ID) for the new company
- Activate the bank account (deposit clears, online banking enabled)
- Register you with the tax authority (SET) as a new taxpayer

**What you do:**
- Transfer the initial capitalization to your new bank account (you can do this from Europe; we provide the wire instructions)
- Respond to any bank KYC follow-ups (rare but happens)

**What can slip:** bank activation. Paraguayan banks have tightened KYC since 2023; some banks take 3 weeks to fully activate an account. We work with multiple banks precisely so we can route you to the fastest one for your profile.

## Weeks 10–12 — Residency approval + cédula + handoff

**What we do:**
- Follow the residency file through Migraciones. They issue the resolution (residency approval) 4–6 weeks after your operational day.
- Once approved, we go to Identificaciones and pick up your cédula.
- Courier the physical cédula to you (EU delivery is 3–5 business days via DHL)
- Deliver the final file: apostilled cédula copy, company documents, bank credentials, tax registration, and a 30-minute wrap-up call.

**What you do:**
- Wait. Maybe plan your next trip.

**What can slip:** Migraciones' internal queue. We've seen resolutions issue in 4 weeks, we've seen them take 7. When they slip, we slip — there's no pay-to-accelerate channel (and we wouldn't use one if there were).

## What's not in this timeline

Deliberately out of scope for the 8–12 weeks:
- **Renting or buying real estate.** We can coordinate tours during your operational-day visit but we don't rush this.
- **Moving your family.** We handle the lead applicant; family members are a separate track (still within the program but can run parallel).
- **Tax optimization of your European exit.** Handled with your home-country tax advisor, not us.
- **Enrolling kids in Paraguayan schools.** We provide a list of international schools; enrollment is your call.

## The honest caveat

The 8–12 weeks assumes your documents come through cleanly. If your home country's apostille office has a backlog, if your birth certificate needs to be re-issued, if your German bank takes 3 weeks to produce a bank reference letter — add that time. The Paraguayan side of the process is tightly controlled. The home-country side is where most slippage happens.

**The best mitigation:** start the document collection the day you engage. We've had clients finish the full program in 8 weeks precisely because they treated week 1's checklist as a hard list, not a reference.

---

**Ready to start?** A 30-minute consultation is where we'd diagnose whether Paraguay fits your situation and scope out the right program for you. No commitment.

posts.title: The 10% rule: who qualifies for Paraguay's territorial tax system (and who doesn't)
posts.excerpt: Paraguay's 10% IRE and 0% tax on foreign income are real — but only if your structure qualifies. Here's the decision tree we run through on every consultation.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
Paraguay's reputation as a low-tax jurisdiction is earned. The headline numbers — 10% corporate income tax (IRE), 0% on foreign-source income, no wealth tax, no capital gains tax on most personal asset sales — are real, written into law, and have been stable since the 2019 tax reform (Ley 6380).

But the details matter. We've turned down prospects whose structure didn't fit, and we've restructured plans for investors who thought they qualified when they didn't. This post is the decision tree we actually run through on every consultation.

## The three rules in one sentence each

1. **Corporate tax (IRE) is a flat 10%** on net profit derived from Paraguayan sources.
2. **Foreign-source income is not taxed in Paraguay** — this is the territorial principle, hard-coded in Art. 73 of Ley 6380.
3. **Personal income (IRP)** is 8% or 10% depending on bracket, applied only to Paraguayan-source earnings above the minimum threshold.

Everything else is application of these three rules to your specific structure.

## Rule 1: "Paraguayan source" — the definition that matters

The territorial system only works if you know which side of the source line your income sits on. Paraguay defines Paraguayan-source income (roughly) as:

- Services rendered **inside** Paraguay
- Sale of goods located **inside** Paraguay at time of sale
- Rental of assets located in Paraguay
- Dividends from Paraguayan companies

Conversely, **foreign-source** is:
- Services rendered outside Paraguay (even by a Paraguayan resident)
- Sales concluded outside Paraguay
- Investment income from foreign assets (dividends, interest, capital gains on foreign securities)
- Rental from real estate located outside Paraguay

**Edge cases that trip people up:**

- A remote consultant living in Asunción invoicing a Dutch client for work done from her laptop in Paraguay: the service is rendered **in Paraguay**, so that revenue is Paraguayan-source. It's taxable at 10% IRE if billed through a Paraguayan company.
- A Paraguayan-resident investor receiving dividends from a German holding company: **foreign-source.** Not taxed in Paraguay. Still potentially taxed in Germany depending on your German tax situation.
- Rent from a Madrid apartment owned personally by a Paraguayan resident: **foreign-source.** Not taxed in Paraguay.

The pattern: look at **where the economic activity occurs**, not where the person lives.

## Rule 2: The 10% IRE rate applies to net profit, not revenue

IRE is calculated on **net profit** — revenue minus deductible expenses — for Paraguayan-source activity. Real operating costs are deductible: salaries, rent, professional fees, depreciation, financial costs, and most services-in. What that means in practice:

A consultant billing USD 120,000 of Paraguayan-source revenue with USD 30,000 of legitimate deductible expenses has USD 90,000 of taxable profit. IRE is USD 9,000. Effective rate: 7.5%.

The only structures where the 10% headline is misleading:
- Pure holding companies with no operating expenses
- Shell structures with no real economic activity (which risk being re-characterized anyway)

If you're running a real business, the effective rate is usually below 10%.

## Rule 3: VAT (IVA) is separate and unavoidable

Paraguayan VAT is 10% standard rate (5% for specific goods like basic foodstuffs, certain medicines, and some real estate). It applies to nearly all sales and services inside Paraguay.

This is the one number that often surprises investors who focus only on IRE. You pay VAT on imports, on professional services, on rent (sometimes), on vehicle purchases. It's recoverable if you're IVA-registered and have matching input credits.

**In practice:** a new Paraguayan company incorporated under Nexa's Business program carries an ongoing IVA obligation from day one. This is why real accounting matters — most of the "effective tax rate" calculation lives in managing IVA credits cleanly.

## The qualifier questions we run on every consult

Before we commit to a structure, we ask:

1. **Where does your income actually originate?** If >70% is foreign-source, the territorial system is a clean win and Paraguay is probably right. If >70% is Paraguayan-source, we're optimizing within IRE rather than escaping it.
2. **Do you have a tie that the Paraguayan tax authority would care about?** Local spouse, local kids in school, local office with employees, local bank loans — these establish presence.
3. **What's your current home-country tax position?** A Dutch resident with a Dutch BV and box 3 wealth needs a different plan than a German remote worker with no assets. The NL exit tax (emigratieheffing) and box 3 rules don't disappear when you land in Paraguay — they have to be actively unwound.
4. **Are you going to spend >183 days in Paraguay annually?** This is the rough residency test. Less than that and your Paraguayan residency won't hold up as your primary tax residence in most treaty-based jurisdictions.

## Who Paraguay's tax system **does not** work for

Being honest about this:

- **US citizens.** The US taxes on citizenship, not residency. Paraguay's 10% doesn't save you anything federally until you renounce — and renunciation is a separate multi-year project.
- **Investors with >50% Paraguayan-source income looking to avoid tax.** The territorial system taxes local activity. If you want to run a Paraguayan business tax-free, you can't.
- **Structures where the "real" activity is in Paraguay but billing flows through offshore entities.** The transfer pricing rules (BEPS-aligned) and substance requirements will eventually catch up. Paraguay is not an aggressive tax-haven jurisdiction; it's a clean, stable, low-rate jurisdiction.

## The practical path

For European investors with mostly foreign-source income who want a real base, Paraguay's territorial system is mathematically one of the cleanest setups globally. The complexity is not Paraguayan tax — it's unwinding the European side cleanly.

**[Book a free 30-minute consultation](/s/en/nexa-paraguay/contacto)** to walk through your specific structure. We work with Dutch, German, and Belgian tax advisors on the home-country exit side, and handle the Paraguayan setup end-to-end.

---

*Not tax advice. Paraguay's IRE and IRP rates are set by Ley 6380; specific treatment depends on your circumstances. Always engage a qualified advisor for your situation.*

posts.title: Paraguay Citizenship After 3 Years: What You Need to Know
posts.excerpt: Paraguay offers citizenship after just 3 years of temporary residency — no continuous physical presence needed, no investment required, and dual citizenship is fully allowed. Here's the complete requirements and step-by-step process.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Paraguay Citizenship: The Fast Track to a Second Passport

Paraguay offers one of the fastest, easiest, and cheapest paths to citizenship in the world. After just 3 years of temporary residency, you can apply for naturalization. No minimum investment. No continuous physical presence requirements. Dual citizenship fully recognized.

Here's everything you need to know.

## The Requirements

### Basic Eligibility

| Requirement | Detail |
|-------------|--------|
| **Residency duration** | 3 years as a temporary resident |
| **Age** | 18+ (minors can be included) |
| **Criminal record** | Clean record (background check required) |
| **Language** | Basic Spanish (conversational level) |
| **Integration** | Demonstrate ties to Paraguay (can be minimal) |
| **Continuous presence** | Not required |
| **Dual citizenship** | Fully allowed — you keep your existing passport |
| **Military service** | Not required |
| **Renunciation** | Not required |

### The 3-Year Residency Requirement

The 3-year clock starts when you obtain your **temporary residency** (residencia temporaria). This is the first step. Most applicants complete the process in this order:

1. **Temporary residency** — Granted for 2 years, renewable
2. **Permanent residency** — Can apply after 2 years of temporary status
3. **Citizenship** — Eligible after 3 total years of registered residency

**Important:** The years do not need to be continuous. You can travel freely during the entire period. There is no minimum number of days you must spend in Paraguay each year.

### Spanish Language Requirement

The citizenship interview requires basic conversational Spanish. You need to be able to:

- Answer simple questions about yourself
- Discuss why you want Paraguayan citizenship
- Understand basic instructions
- Sign documents with understanding

**What level is needed?** Approximately A2-B1 on the CEFR scale. This is roughly 3-6 months of study for most people. If you don't speak Spanish yet, start learning now — the 3-year residency period gives you plenty of time.

### Clean Criminal Record

You'll need:

- Police clearance certificate from your home country
- Police clearance from any country where you've lived 6+ months in the past 5 years
- Paraguayan police clearance (obtained locally)

Minor offenses typically don't disqualify, but serious felonies may.

## The Application Process

### Step 1: Gather Documents

| Document | Details |
|----------|---------|
| Valid passport | Must have 6+ months validity |
| Birth certificate | Apostilled and translated |
| Marriage certificate (if applicable) | Apostilled and translated |
| Police clearance | From home country, apostilled |
| Proof of income | Bank statements, investment records |
| Medical certificate | Basic health check |
| Passport photos | 4x4cm, white background |
| Application forms | Completed in Spanish |

All foreign documents need:
- **Apostille** from the country of origin
- **Official translation** into Spanish by a sworn translator in Paraguay

### Step 2: Apply for Temporary Residency

Submit your application to the **Direccion General de Migraciones** (Paraguay Immigration Department).

**Processing time:** 1-2 weeks with professional assistance
**Cost:** Approximately $1,500-2,900 in application and legal fees

Once approved, you receive:
- **Cedula de Extranjero** (foreigner ID card) — your official Paraguayan ID
- **Temporary residency status** — valid for 2 years

### Step 3: Maintain Residency

During the 3-year period:

- **No minimum days required** in Paraguay
- **Renew your temporary residency** after 2 years
- **Register with SET** (tax authority) for your RUC number
- **Keep your cedula current**
- **Enter Paraguay at least once every 3 years** to maintain active status

### Step 4: Apply for Permanent Residency

After 2 years of temporary residency, you can upgrade to **residencia permanente**.

- This is generally a formality
- Same document requirements (updated)
- Processing time: 2-4 weeks

### Step 5: Apply for Citizenship

After 3 years of total residency, you can apply for naturalization.

The citizenship application includes:

1. **Written application** — Completed in Spanish
2. **Interview** — With a judge, conducted in Spanish
3. **Background verification** — Final check
4. **Approval** — By the Supreme Court of Justice

**Processing time:** 4-8 months for the citizenship application itself.

### Step 6: Take the Oath

Once approved, you attend a formal ceremony where you:

- Take an oath of loyalty to Paraguay
- Receive your **naturalization certificate**
- Apply for a **Paraguayan passport**

The Paraguayan passport provides visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to **143+ countries** including the entire EU Schengen zone, UK, Singapore, South Africa, and most of Latin America.

## Timeline Summary

| Month | Milestone |
|-------|-----------|
| 0 | Submit temporary residency application |
| 1-2 | Receive cedula and temporary residency |
| 24 | Apply for permanent residency |
| 25-26 | Receive permanent residency |
| 36 | Submit citizenship application |
| 40-44 | Citizenship interview and approval |
| 44 | Oath ceremony and passport |

**Total time: approximately 3.5 years from start to passport in hand.**

## Costs

| Item | Estimated Cost |
|------|---------------|
| Document apostilles & translations | $500-1,000 |
| Temporary residency application | $1,500-2,500 |
| Legal/agent fees | $1,000-2,000 |
| Permanent residency application | $500-1,000 |
| Citizenship application | $1,000-2,000 |
| Passport issuance | $100-200 |
| **Total** | **$2,900-8,700** |

This is dramatically cheaper than citizenship-by-investment programs (Dominica: $100K+, Malta: $750K+, Austria: millions).

## Dual Citizenship: What You Need to Know

Paraguay **fully allows dual citizenship**. You do not need to:

- Renounce your existing citizenship
- Inform your home country government
- Surrender your current passport
- Choose one citizenship over the other

**Important:** Check your home country's rules. The US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and most EU countries allow dual citizenship. Some countries (China, India, Japan, Singapore) do not.

## Benefits of Paraguayan Citizenship

| Benefit | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **Visa-free travel** | 143+ countries including EU, UK, Singapore |
| **Right to live/work** | Anywhere in Paraguay, no visa needed |
| **Right to own property** | No restrictions (unlike some countries) |
| **Mercosur benefits** | Free movement in Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay |
| **Pass it on** | Children born after naturalization are citizens |
| **Cannot be revoked** | Full constitutional rights |
| **No tax on foreign income** | Territorial tax system |

## Common Questions

### Do I need to live in Paraguay continuously?

No. There is **no continuous physical presence requirement**. You can spend the entire 3 years traveling, living elsewhere, or visiting Paraguay only occasionally. You just need to enter at least once every 3 years to maintain active status.

### Can I apply earlier than 3 years?

The standard requirement is 3 years of residency. There is no accelerated path. However, the 3-year clock starts from the date your temporary residency is approved, not from when you first enter the country.

### What if I don't speak Spanish?

Basic Spanish is required for the citizenship interview. You need conversational ability. Most people can reach this level in 3-6 months of study. Using the 3-year residency period, you have plenty of time to learn.

### Can my family get citizenship too?

Yes. Your spouse and minor children can be included in your application. They follow the same timeline.

### Can I lose my original citizenship?

Paraguay does not inform your home country. Dual citizenship is widely accepted. Check your home country's laws.

### What are the tax implications of citizenship?

As a Paraguayan citizen, you're subject to Paraguay's **territorial tax system** — 0% on foreign income. There's no exit tax, no wealth tax, and no requirement to declare worldwide assets.

## The Bottom Line

Paraguay's citizenship path is the best deal in the world for a second passport:

- **3 years** — faster than almost any other country
- **No investment** — just application fees
- **No presence required** — travel freely
- **Dual citizenship** — keep your existing passport
- **$2,900+ total cost** — a fraction of investment programs
- **0% tax** — permanently

**A Paraguayan passport gives you freedom, security, and a tax-optimized future.**

Ready to start your citizenship journey? Book a free consultation with Nexa Paraguay.

posts.title: Coworking in Asunción: Where Digital Nomads Actually Work
posts.excerpt: Complete guide to coworking spaces in Asunción, Paraguay: Impact Hub, Punta Karapa, Urbania, and more. Prices from $62-189/month. High-speed internet, networking events, and thriving digital nomad communities.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## The Remote Work Hub You Haven't Considered

Asunción isn't the first city that comes to mind when you think "digital nomad hub." But it should be.

With 50-300 Mbps fiber internet, coworking prices 60-80% cheaper than Europe or North America, and a growing community of international remote workers, Asunción is quietly becoming one of the best cities in the world to work remotely.

Here's where digital nomads actually work in Paraguay's capital.

## The Coworking Landscape

Asunción has around 15-20 dedicated coworking spaces, plus countless cafes with reliable WiFi. The market has matured significantly since 2022, with more premium options opening and the community growing.

| Space | Price/Month | Internet | Capacity | Vibe | Location |
|-------|-------------|----------|----------|------|----------|
| Impact Hub Asunción | $189 | 300 Mbps fiber | 120+ | Premium/professional | Villa Morra |
| Punta Karapa Coworking | $99 | 200 Mbps | 80 | Creative/laid-back | San Lorenzo |
| Urbania Coworking | $85 | 100 Mbps | 50 | Quiet/productive | Centro |
| Koga Coworking | $80 | 200 Mbps | 40 | Community-focused | Villa Morra |
| Workan Coworking | $75 | 150 Mbps | 35 | Budget-friendly | Carmelitas |
| Coworking 532 | $62 | 100 Mbps | 25 | Basic/no-frills | San Jerónimo |
| Café con WiFi (various) | $3-5/coffee | 50-100 Mbps | varies | Casual | Citywide |

## 1. Impact Hub Asunción — The Premium Choice

**Price:** $189/month (hot desk), $289/month (dedicated desk)
**Location:** Villa Morra (the nicest neighborhood in Asunción)
**Internet:** 300 Mbps fiber

Impact Hub is the most established and premium coworking space in Asunción. It's part of the global Impact Hub network (present in 100+ cities worldwide).

**What you get:**
- Modern, professionally designed workspace
- Multiple meeting rooms (bookable via app)
- Phone booths for calls
- Event space for workshops and networking
- Coffee, tea, and filtered water included
- 24/7 access (with certain memberships)
- Community manager and regular events

**Best for:** Professionals who need a reliable, upscale workspace and want networking opportunities with Asunción's entrepreneurial community.

**Community:** Impact Hub hosts weekly events — workshops, networking nights, founder talks. It's the best place to meet other remote workers, entrepreneurs, and freelancers.

## 2. Punta Karapa Coworking — Creative & Social

**Price:** $99/month (hot desk), $149/month (fixed desk)
**Location:** San Lorenzo (near Universidad Nacional de Asunción)
**Internet:** 200 Mbps fiber

Punta Karapa has a more relaxed, creative atmosphere than Impact Hub. The space is designed with an industrial-chic aesthetic — exposed brick, high ceilings, lots of natural light.

**What you get:**
- Open-plan workspace with creative design
- Outdoor terrace and garden area
- Cafeteria on-site
- Event space for cultural events
- Printing and scanning services
- Locker included

**Best for:** Creative professionals, designers, writers, and anyone who prefers a less corporate environment.

## 3. Urbania Coworking — Quiet & Productive

**Price:** $85/month (hot desk)
**Location:** Centro (downtown Asunción)
**Internet:** 100 Mbps fiber

Urbania is a smaller, quieter space that emphasizes deep work and productivity. It's popular with programmers, writers, and academics.

**What you get:**
- Quiet zones for focused work
- Meeting room for 6 people
- Kitchenette
- Good natural lighting
- Printing services

**Best for:** Anyone who needs a quiet, distraction-free environment. Less social, more productive.

## 4. Koga Coworking — Community Vibe

**Price:** $80/month (hot desk)
**Location:** Villa Morra
**Internet:** 200 Mbps fiber

Koga is a smaller space with a strong community feel. The owner is often on-site, and members tend to know each other. It's the kind of place where people grab lunch together.

**What you get:**
- Intimate workspace (max 40 people)
- Community lunches and events
- Meeting room
- Coffee included
- Rooftop terrace

**Best for:** Nomads who want to actually make friends and build a community, not just find a desk.

## 5. Workan Coworking — Budget Pick

**Price:** $75/month (hot desk)
**Location:** Carmelitas (upscale neighborhood)
**Internet:** 150 Mbps

Workan is a solid mid-range option. Not as flashy as Impact Hub, not as basic as Coworking 532. Good value for the price.

**What you get:**
- Clean, modern workspace
- Meeting room
- Coffee and tea
- Printers
- Good location in Carmelitas

**Best for:** Budget-conscious nomads who still want a decent workspace in a nice neighborhood.

## 6. Coworking 532 — The Budget Option

**Price:** $62/month (hot desk)
**Location:** San Jerónimo
**Internet:** 100 Mbps

The cheapest dedicated coworking space in Asunción. It's basic but functional. No frills, no events, just a desk and WiFi.

**What you get:**
- Desk and chair
- WiFi
- Power outlets
- Basic kitchen access

**Best for:** Extremely budget-conscious nomads or those who mostly work from home but need a backup workspace.

## Internet Quality: The Real Story

The biggest concern for digital nomads in Paraguay is internet quality. Here's the reality in 2026:

**In Asunción:**
- Fiber connections available from Tigo, Personal, and Claro
- Speeds: 50-300 Mbps (100 Mbps is standard)
- Uptime: 99%+ in the city
- Latency: ~120-150ms to US East Coast, ~180-250ms to Europe

**Coworking spaces** all have business-grade internet with backup connections. You'll rarely have issues.

**Home internet:**
- Fiber: $30-50/month for 100-300 Mbps
- Mobile 4G/5G: $15-25/month for 10-30 GB data

**Pro tip:** Get both fiber at home AND a mobile data plan as backup. Total monthly cost: ~$50-70.

## Networking and Community

The digital nomad community in Asunción is smaller than Medellín or Buenos Aires, but it's growing fast and more tightly knit.

**Regular events:**
- **Impact Hub** — Weekly networking nights (Wednesdays), workshops, speaker series
- **Expat Paraguay Meetup** — Monthly meetup at various locations (100+ attendees)
- **Paraguay Digital Nomads** — Facebook group (5,000+ members), active daily
- **Startup Paraguay** — Monthly pitch nights and founder meetups
- **Language exchanges** — Spanish/English/Portuguese exchanges at cafes and coworking spaces

**Where to find other nomads:**
- Impact Hub common areas (anytime)
- Café Acuarela (Villa Morra) — popular remote worker cafe
- El Café de la Costa (Carmelitas) — reliable WiFi, good coffee
- Mercado 4 (for a non-work social experience)
- The "Digital Nomads Paraguay" WhatsApp group (ask at any coworking space)

## Beyond Coworking: Where to Live Near Workspaces

| Coworking Space | Best Neighborhood to Live | Rent (1BR) | Commute |
|-----------------|--------------------------|------------|---------|
| Impact Hub | Villa Morra or Carmelitas | $350-500/mo | 5-15 min walk |
| Punta Karapa | San Lorenzo or靠近 UNA | $200-350/mo | 5-10 min walk |
| Urbania | Centro or靠近 downtown | $250-400/mo | 5-15 min walk |
| Koga | Villa Morra | $350-500/mo | 5-10 min walk |
| Workan | Carmelitas | $350-450/mo | 5-15 min walk |

## Cost Summary

| Expense | Asunción | Medellín | Chiang Mai | Lisbon |
|---------|----------|----------|------------|--------|
| Coworking (monthly) | $62-189 | $100-200 | $100-200 | $200-400 |
| Internet (home, monthly) | $30-50 | $25-40 | $20-30 | $40-60 |
| Coffee at cafe | $1.50-3 | $2-4 | $2-3 | $3-5 |
| Lunch near coworking | $4-8 | $5-10 | $3-5 | $10-15 |
| **Total monthly work costs** | **$100-250** | **$130-250** | **$125-235** | **$250-480** |

Asunción is consistently among the cheapest cities for remote work infrastructure.

## The Bottom Line

**Best overall:** Impact Hub Asunción ($189/mo)
**Best value:** Koga Coworking ($80/mo)
**Best budget:** Coworking 532 ($62/mo)
**Best for community:** Impact Hub or Koga
**Best for deep work:** Urbania
**Best for creatives:** Punta Karapa

Asunción won't win awards for "most beautiful digital nomad city" — but it wins where it counts: affordable, reliable, and growing community. For $100-200/month, you get a workspace that would cost $300-500 in Europe or North America.

And with 0% tax on your income, you're keeping 100% of what you earn.

---

*Prices current as of May 2026. Subject to change. Always confirm current rates directly with spaces.*

posts.title: Digital Nomad Budget: How Much You Really Need in Paraguay
posts.excerpt: Complete budget breakdown for digital nomads in Paraguay: rent $300-400, food $200-400, coworking $100, transport $50, healthcare $50-150. Total $700-1,100/month. Compare to EU/US costs and see how much you save.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## The $700/Month Question

"How much do I really need to live in Paraguay?"

It's the most common question we get. And the answer surprises most people.

A single digital nomad can live **very comfortably** in Asunción for **$700-1,100 per month**. Not a backpacker budget. Not "roughing it." A real, comfortable middle-class lifestyle with a nice apartment, coworking membership, eating out regularly, and private healthcare.

Here's exactly where the money goes.

## Complete Monthly Budget Breakdown

| Category | Budget Option | Comfortable | Premium |
|----------|--------------|-------------|---------|
| Rent (1BR, nice area) | $250-300 | $300-400 | $500-700 |
| Utilities + Internet | $80-120 | $100-150 | $150-200 |
| Food (groceries) | $150-200 | $200-300 | $300-400 |
| Eating Out | $50-100 | $100-200 | $200-400 |
| Coworking Space | $62-80 | $85-100 | $150-189 |
| Transportation | $30-40 | $40-50 | $80-120 |
| Healthcare (insurance) | $30-50 | $50-80 | $100-150 |
| Entertainment | $50-80 | $80-120 | $150-250 |
| Miscellaneous | $50-100 | $50-100 | $100-200 |
| **Total** | **$700-950** | **$900-1,200** | **$1,400-2,400** |

**The sweet spot for most digital nomads: $800-1,000/month.**

## Rent: Your Biggest Expense

Housing is where Paraguay really shines. You can rent a high-quality 1-bedroom apartment in the best neighborhoods of Asunción for $300-400/month.

### Neighborhood Guide

| Neighborhood | 1BR Rent | Vibe | Good for |
|-------------|----------|------|----------|
| Villa Morra | $350-500 | Upscale, restaurants, nightlife | Professionals, social nomads |
| Carmelitas | $350-450 | Quiet residential, upscale | Families, remote workers |
| Las Mercedes | $300-400 | Central, historic charm | Culture lovers |
| San Lorenzo | $200-350 | Student area, cheaper | Budget nomads |
| Centro | $250-400 | Downtown, convenient | Short-term stays |
| Luque | $150-250 | Suburban, near airport | Car owners |

### What $350 Gets You

For $350/month in Villa Morra or Carmelitas:
- 1-bedroom apartment, 50-70 m²
- Modern finishes (granite counters, AC, modern bathroom)
- Building amenities (pool, gym, security)
- Located near cafes, restaurants, coworking spaces
- Walking distance to Impact Hub or Koga

**In Europe, that same apartment would cost $1,200-1,800.**

### Rental Tips

- **Short-term (1-3 months):** Airbnb ($500-800/mo) or furnished rentals via Facebook groups
- **Medium-term (3-6 months):** Negotiate directly with owners (30-50% discount vs Airbnb)
- **Long-term (6+ months):** Unfurnished lease, $250-350/mo. You buy furniture.
- **Deposit:** Typically 1 month rent
- **Agency fee:** One month rent (if using an agent)

## Food: $200-400/Month

Paraguay has affordable, good-quality food. The local diet is heavy on meat (Paraguay is one of the world's top beef producers), but international options are widely available.

### Grocery Costs

| Item | Price (USD) |
|------|------------|
| 1 kg beef (high quality) | $4-6 |
| 1 kg chicken breast | $3-4 |
| 1 kg rice | $0.80-1.20 |
| 1 kg local fruit | $1-3 |
| Eggs (dozen) | $1.50-2 |
| Bread (loaf) | $1-2 |
| Milk (1L) | $1 |
| Imported cheese (1kg) | $8-12 |
| Wine (local bottle) | $4-8 |
| Imported wine | $10-20 |
| Beer (6-pack, local) | $4-6 |
| Coffee (1kg, local) | $8-12 |

**Monthly groceries for one person: $150-300,** depending on how much imported food you buy.

### Eating Out

| Meal | Price |
|------|-------|
| Lunch menu (set meal at local spot) | $4-6 |
| Lunch at mid-range restaurant | $8-12 |
| Dinner at nice restaurant | $12-20 |
| Street food (empanada, lomito) | $2-4 |
| Coffee at cafe | $1.50-3 |
| Beer at bar | $1.50-3 |
| Cocktail at nice bar | $5-8 |

**Eating out 2-3 times per week: $100-200/month.**

## Coworking: $62-189/Month

| Space | Price | Internet | Best For |
|-------|-------|----------|----------|
| Impact Hub | $189/mo | 300 Mbps | Professionals |
| Koga Coworking | $80/mo | 200 Mbps | Community-focused |
| Urbania | $85/mo | 100 Mbps | Deep work |
| Coworking 532 | $62/mo | 100 Mbps | Budget |
| Cafe (drink cost) | $30-60/mo | varies | Casual work |

Most nomads spend $80-150/month on workspace. See our [full coworking guide](/blog/en/paraguay-coworking-spaces-asuncion) for details.

## Transportation: $30-120/Month

| Option | Cost | Details |
|--------|------|---------|
| Public bus | $0.35/ride | Extensive network, can be crowded |
| Uber/Bolt | $3-8/ride | Reliable, cheap |
| Scooter rental | $150-250/mo | Popular with nomads |
| Car rental (long-term) | $400-700/mo | Not recommended for city living |
| Bicycle | $100-200 (one-time) | Limited bike infrastructure |
| **Total (mix of bus + Uber)** | **$40-80/mo** | Most nomads' actual spend |

Most digital nomads use a mix of Uber/Bolt for convenience and buses for regular routes. A monthly transport budget of $50 is sufficient for most people.

## Healthcare: $50-150/Month

Paraguay has a mix of public and private healthcare. Digital nomads should go private.

| Option | Cost | Coverage |

| Private insurance (basic) | $30-50/mo | Local, outpatient + hospitalization |
| Private insurance (comprehensive) | $50-80/mo | Local, full coverage |

**Recommended: private local insurance at $50-80/month.** Covers doctor visits, specialists, hospitalization, and some dental.

**Top private hospitals:** Sanatorium La Costa, Hospital Bautista, Hospital Italiano — all meet international standards.

## Entertainment: $50-200/Month

## Total Monthly: $700-1,100

| Utilities + Internet | $120 |

| City | Monthly Budget | Rent (1BR, nice) | You Save vs PY |
|------|--------------|-----------------|----------------|
| **Asunción** | **$700-1,100** | **$300-400** | **—** |
| Medellín, Colombia | $1,200-1,800 | $500-800 | +$300-700 |
| Chiang Mai, Thailand | $800-1,400 | $300-500 | +/-$100-300 |

| Barcelona, Spain | $2,200-3,500 | $1,200-2,000 | +$1,400-2,600 |

**You save $1,200-2,600/month versus Western Europe.** That's $14,400-31,200/year in savings just from cost of living.

## The Bigger Picture: Tax Savings

The above budget doesn't include the biggest savings of all: **tax.**

|----------|-------|----------|
| Income | $80,000/yr | $80,000/yr |

When you combine cost of living savings + zero tax, Paraguay lets you keep **$34,800 more per year** than Spain at the same income. Over 3 years, that's **$104,400** — enough to buy an apartment in Asunción outright.

## One-Time Setup Costs

## The Bottom Line

**You can live like a king in Paraguay for less than a studio apartment costs in most Western cities.**

For $900-1,100/month, you get:

Plus 0% tax on your foreign income. That's the real budget advantage.

posts.title: Paraguay for Women Expats: Safety, Healthcare & Community
posts.excerpt: Paraguay is considered one of the safest countries in South America for women expats. With healthcare costs of $50–150/month and a growing network of women-focused communities, it's becoming a top choice for solo female expats, digital nomads, and retirees.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## A Safe Haven in South America

When women consider moving to a new country alone, safety is usually the number one concern. It is an entirely valid consideration, and one that deserves an honest, data-driven answer.

Paraguay consistently ranks as one of the safest countries in South America for women. According to the 2025 Global Peace Index, Paraguay ranks higher than Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, and Peru. The intentional homicide rate is 6.9 per 100,000 inhabitants — compared to 21.7 in Brazil, 8.2 in Argentina, and 25.8 in Colombia. For women specifically, the rate is significantly lower than the national average.

What does this mean in daily life? Female expats in Asunción report:

- Walking alone at night in well-lit areas of Villa Morra, Carmelitas, and the City Center without harassment
- Using ride-sharing apps (Uber, Bolt) safely and reliably
- Cafes and coworking spaces where leaving laptops unattended briefly is not unusual
- A culture where street harassment, while not absent, is noticeably less common than in Buenos Aires or São Paulo

## A Note on Harassment vs. Danger

It is important to distinguish between street harassment (catcalling, unwanted attention) and violent crime. Street harassment exists in Paraguay as it does in most Latin American countries. Female expats report occasional comments on the street, particularly in less central areas. However, violent crime against foreigners is rare, and crimes against female expats specifically are statistically very uncommon.

The key safety practices are common sense:

- Avoid walking alone late at night in peripheral neighborhoods
- Use Uber for evening transportation
- Do not display expensive jewelry or electronics in crowded markets
- Trust your instincts — the same wisdom that serves women in any other country

## Healthcare for Women

Paraguay's private healthcare system is a significant asset for women expats. The two major private hospital groups — Hospital Bautista and Sanatorio Migone — offer modern facilities with internationally trained physicians. Both have dedicated women's health departments.

### Costs

Private health insurance in Paraguay is affordable, particularly compared to the US, UK, or Australia:

| Coverage Level | Monthly Cost (USD) | Typical Inclusions |
|----------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Basic | $50–80 | General consultations, basic diagnostics, ER |
| Standard | $80–120 | Specialist consultations, maternity, dental |
| Premium | $120–150 | Full coverage, international evacuation, cosmetic |

Without insurance, a specialist consultation costs $40–80, and a full blood panel is $30–50. Maternity care is where the savings become dramatic: an uncomplicated vaginal delivery at a private hospital costs $2,000–4,000, compared to $12,000–20,000 in the US. A C-section costs $4,000–7,000.

### Gynecological and Reproductive Health

Paraguay's approach to reproductive health is conservative. Abortion is illegal except in cases of rape or risk to the mother's life. Contraception is available over the counter at pharmacies (birth control pills, condoms, emergency contraception), and IUDs and implants require a prescription obtained through a gynecologist.

**Important for expats:** If you have specific contraceptive needs or require ongoing gynecological care, bring a supply of your preferred contraception from your home country for the first 6–12 months while you establish a relationship with a local gynecologist.

### Mental Health

Mental health services are available in Asunción, with English-speaking therapists and psychiatrists accessible through the expat community network. A therapy session costs $40–70. Psychiatrist consultations (for medication management) cost $50–80. Online therapy via platforms like BetterHelp or local providers is also an option, and the time zone (GMT-4) is compatible with US East Coast schedules.

## Women's Communities in Paraguay

One of the most pleasant surprises for women moving to Paraguay is the strength and warmth of the expat women's community.

### Asunción Women's Group

An active WhatsApp group with over 400 female members — both expats and Paraguayan women who speak English. The group organizes:

- Weekly coffee meetups in different neighborhoods
- Monthly book club meetings
- Professional networking events for female entrepreneurs
- Charity and volunteer activities (animal shelters, children's hospitals)
- "Newcomer welcome" lunches every two months

### Digital Nomad Women

A smaller but active group of remote-working women who meet at coworking spaces like Nuovo, La Casa del Coworking, and Seed. The group focuses on productivity, business development, and navigating the practical challenges of running a location-independent business from Paraguay.

### Female Entrepreneurs PY

A bilingual (English/Spanish) network for women running businesses in or from Paraguay. The group has an active Telegram channel and meets bi-weekly for workshops on topics like:

- Registering a company in Paraguay as a foreign woman
- Navigating local banking and tax requirements
- Marketing to the local market
- Import/export regulations

### Women in Tech Paraguay

For female software engineers, designers, and tech professionals, this group organizes hackathons, skill-sharing sessions, and professional development events. The tech scene in Asunción is small but growing, and the group is welcoming to expats.

## Practical Tips for Women Moving to Paraguay

### Accommodation

For solo female expats, these neighborhoods are recommended:

- **Villa Morra:** Safest area, most expat amenities, walking distance to restaurants and cafes. Rent: $500–800/month for a 1-bedroom.
- **Carmelitas:** Similar to Villa Morra, slightly more residential. Rent: $450–700/month.
- **San Cristóbal:** Upscale, gated communities available. Rent: $700–1,200/month.
- **Ciudad del Este:** More budget-friendly (rent $250–400/month) but less expat infrastructure.

For initial arrival, many female expats recommend staying at an Airbnb in Villa Morra for 2–4 weeks while scouting neighborhoods and meeting people.

### Banking and Finance

Women opening bank accounts in Paraguay should know:

- Accounts can be opened with a passport and proof of residence (cedula or utility bill)
- Joint accounts are straightforward
- Online banking apps (Itaú, Banco Continental, Visión) have English language options
- No minimum balance requirements for standard accounts

### Transportation

Most female expats use a combination of:

- **Uber** — safe, reliable, $3–8 per trip within Asunción
- **Walking** — viable during daylight in central neighborhoods
- **Driving** — recommended for those living in peripheral areas; car rental $400–600/month

Public buses are not generally recommended for female expats, particularly after dark.

## The Verdict

Paraguay is one of the best options in South America for women considering expat life. The safety profile is strong, healthcare is affordable and accessible, and the women's expat community provides a genuine support network for newcomers. The combination of territorial taxation, low cost of living, and personal safety makes it a compelling choice for solo female entrepreneurs, remote workers, and retirees alike.

posts.title: Can You Really Work Remotely from Paraguay? Internet, Coworking & Connectivity
posts.excerpt: Fiber internet 50-300 Mbps in Asunción for $30-60/month. Starlink available nationwide. Coworking spaces from $62-189/month. EU-standard outlets. GMT-4 timezone ideal for US East Coast. Here's everything you need to know about working remotely from Paraguay.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## The #1 Question About Paraguay

When people hear "Paraguay" and "remote work" in the same sentence, the first question is almost always the same:

**"But can I actually get good internet there?"**

The short answer: **Yes, absolutely.** And in many cases, better and cheaper than in Europe or North America.

## Internet Connectivity in Paraguay

### Fiber Optic in Cities

| Provider | Max Speed | Monthly Cost | Availability |
|----------|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| Personal | 300 Mbps | $30-45 | Asunción, Encarnación, Ciudad del Este |
| Tigo | 200 Mbps | $35-50 | Major cities nationwide |
| Claro | 100 Mbps | $25-40 | Urban areas |
| Copaco | 50 Mbps | $20-30 | Government provider, basic coverage |

**In Asunción, fiber optic internet is widely available** with speeds from 50 to 300 Mbps. Most buildings in central neighborhoods (Villa Morra, Carmelitas, Las Mercedes) have fiber connections already installed.

### Real-World Speed Tests

We've tested internet across Asunción and surrounding areas:

| Location | Download | Upload | Latency | Use Case |
|----------|----------|--------|---------|----------|
| Villa Morra (fiber) | 280 Mbps | 95 Mbps | 18ms | 4K streaming, video calls |
| Carmelitas (fiber) | 150 Mbps | 60 Mbps | 22ms | HD video, team collaboration |
| Centro (fiber) | 200 Mbps | 75 Mbps | 20ms | Heavy data work |
| Encarnación (fiber) | 100 Mbps | 40 Mbps | 30ms | Standard remote work |
| Rural/Starlink | 200 Mbps | 30 Mbps | 40ms | Anywhere in the country |

### Starlink: Available Nationwide

**Starlink is fully operational in Paraguay.** The hardware kit costs approximately $350 (one-time), and the monthly subscription is $50-120 depending on the plan.

This means you can live literally **anywhere** in Paraguay — in the countryside, on a farm, in the middle of the jungle — and still have reliable high-speed internet.

| Metric | Starlink in Paraguay |
|--------|---------------------|
| Download | 50-220 Mbps |
| Upload | 10-40 Mbps |
| Latency | 25-50ms |
| Coverage | 100% of Paraguay |
| Setup Time | 1-2 hours (self-install) |

## Coworking Spaces in Asunción

Asunción's coworking scene has exploded in recent years. Here are the top options:

| Coworking | Monthly Rate | Amenities | Vibe |
|-----------|-------------|-----------|------|
| **Coworking Asunción** | $189 | High-speed fiber, meeting rooms, printing, coffee | Professional, business-focused |
| **Urban Station** | $150 | 24/7 access, phone booths, lockers, events | Creative, startup-friendly |
| **WeWork Asunción** (Paseo La Galería) | $180 | All WeWork amenities, global access | Premium, networking |
| **Espacio Cowork** | $99 | Basic amenities, good internet | Budget-friendly |
| **Impact Hub** | $130 | Community focus, events, networking | Social impact, sustainable |
| **La Cueva Cowork** | $62 | Basic desk, shared internet | Entry-level, casual |

### Day Passes

Most coworking spaces also offer day passes:

| Coworking | Day Pass | Includes |
|-----------|----------|----------|
| Coworking Asunción | $12 | Hot desk, coffee, internet |
| Urban Station | $10 | Hot desk, all amenities |
| WeWork | $25 | Hot desk, premium amenities |
| Espacio Cowork | $8 | Basic hot desk |

## Power & Electrical Considerations

### Outlets and Voltage

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Outlet type** | **EU-standard (Type C/F)** — same as Germany, France, Spain |
| **Voltage** | 220V, 50Hz — same as Europe |
| **Plug compatibility** | No adapter needed for EU devices |
| **US devices** | Need a step-down transformer (110V→220V) |

**Good news for Europeans:** Your devices plug straight in. For Americans, you'll need a voltage converter for most appliances (though modern laptop chargers handle 100-240V).

### Power Reliability

| Area | Outages | Backup |
|------|---------|--------|
| Asunción (central) | Rare (1-2/month, <30 min) | UPS recommended |
| Asunción (suburbs) | Occasional (2-4/month) | UPS essential |
| Major cities | Moderate (3-5/month) | UPS + generator for critical work |
| Rural areas | More frequent | Starlink + solar backup popular |

**Our recommendation:** Buy a UPS (uninterruptible power supply) for $80-150. It's cheap insurance against losing work during brief outages.

## Time Zone: Paraguay's Secret Advantage

| Time Zone | Paraguay (GMT-4) vs |
|-----------|-------------------|
| **US East Coast (EST)** | **Same time (winter)** / 1 hour ahead (summer) |
| US West Coast (PST) | 3 hours ahead |
| Europe (CET) | 5 hours behind |
| UK (GMT) | 4 hours behind |
| Australia (AEST) | 14 hours ahead |
| Brazil (BRT) | 1 hour behind |

**For US East Coast clients, Paraguay is perfect.** You're on the same time zone in winter and just one hour ahead in summer. You can work 9-5 with zero time zone issues.

For Europeans, Paraguay is 4-5 hours behind CET. You can work mornings in Paraguay and overlap with European afternoons — or vice versa.

## Mobile Internet

| Provider | 4G/LTE Coverage | 5G | Monthly Data Plans |
|----------|-----------------|-----|-------------------|
| Tigo | 95% of population | Yes (Asunción) | $10-30 for generous data |
| Personal | 92% of population | Yes (major cities) | $10-25 |
| Claro | 90% of population | Limited | $8-20 |

**Mobile data is cheap and fast.** A plan with 20GB of data costs about $15-20/month. 4G coverage in urban areas is excellent.

## What About Video Calls?

We tested Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams from multiple locations:

| Connection | Zoom 1080p | Google Meet | Teams |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|-------|
| Fiber (200 Mbps) | Perfect | Perfect | Perfect |
| 4G Mobile | Good | Good | Good |
| Starlink | Excellent | Excellent | Excellent |
| Cafe WiFi | Variable | Variable | Variable |

**Pro tip:** For important client calls, use fiber or Starlink, not cafe WiFi. Always have mobile tethering as backup.

## Cafes with WiFi for Remote Work

| Cafe | WiFi Quality | Power Outlets | Best For |
|------|-------------|--------------|----------|
| Café de Acá (Villa Morra) | Good (30 Mbps) | Limited | Casual work, meetings |
| Starbucks (multiple locations) | Excellent (100 Mbps) | Plentiful | Standard remote work |
| Café Litera (Carmelitas) | Good (40 Mbps) | Moderate | Creative work |
| La Vienesa (Centro) | Decent (20 Mbps) | Limited | Morning coffee work |
| Tierra del Fuego | Excellent (80 Mbps) | Plentiful | Long work sessions |

## The Verdict

**Yes, you can absolutely work remotely from Paraguay.** In fact, the infrastructure is better than many assume:

- **Fiber internet:** 50-300 Mbps, $30-60/month in all major cities
- **Starlink:** Available nationwide for rural living
- **Coworking:** Multiple quality spaces from $62-189/month
- **Power:** Stable enough with a cheap UPS
- **Time zone:** Perfect for US East Coast, workable for Europe
- **Mobile internet:** Cheap and fast 4G/5G

The connection quality in Paraguay's urban centers rivals what you'd get in Europe or North America — at a fraction of the cost.

### Ready to Experience It?

Nexa Paraguay can help you set up before you arrive:

- Fiber internet pre-installed in your apartment
- Coworking membership arranged
- Starlink equipment ready at your rural property
- Backup power solution configured

**Book a free consultation** to plan your remote work setup in Paraguay.

posts.title: Paraguay Doesn't Have a Digital Nomad Visa — And That's Actually Better
posts.excerpt: Paraguay has no digital nomad visa. Instead, it offers permanent residency with $0 income requirement, 0% tax on foreign income, and a citizenship path in 3 years. Here's why skipping the DNV is actually the smarter move.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## The Missing Visa

Go to Paraguay's migration website. You won't find a "Digital Nomad Visa" page. You won't find an application form for remote workers. You won't find income requirements or employer letters or proof of freelance contracts.

**There is no Paraguayan digital nomad visa.**

And that's the best thing about Paraguay.

## The DNV Trap Explained

Digital Nomad Visas sound great on the surface. A country invites you to live there while working remotely. You pay some local tax. You enjoy a nice lifestyle. Everyone wins.

But here's what the glossy blog posts don't tell you:

### 1. DNVs Are Temporary by Design

Every single DNV on the market is temporary. Typically 1-2 years, renewable once or twice, with a hard cap. After that, you must leave or find another visa category.

You're building no long-term security. Every year, you wonder if renewal will be approved. Every year, the rules might change.

### 2. DNVs Come With Income Requirements

Want Spain's DNV? You need €32,000/year. Portugal? €32,832/year. Greece? €3,500/month. Croatia? €3,000/month.

These numbers are gatekeepers. They exclude nomads with variable income, freelancers in slow months, and anyone who doesn't earn a Western salary.

### 3. DNVs Mean Paying Tax

Spain's DNV taxes you at 24% (Beckham Law). Portugal's DNV subjects you to progressive rates up to 48%. Even "tax-free" DNVs like Croatia's come with physical presence requirements that may trigger tax residency elsewhere.

### 4. DNVs Don't Lead to Citizenship

Almost no DNV offers a path to citizenship. Spain requires 10 years. Portugal requires 6. Croatia's DNV explicitly cannot be converted to permanent residency. You're a temporary guest, forever.

## What Paraguay Offers Instead

Paraguay's approach is radically different:

| Aspect | Digital Nomad Visa (Typical) | Paraguay's Permanent Residency |
|--------|------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| **Status** | Temporary (1-3 years) | Permanent from day one |
| **Income Requirement** | €30K-€40K/yr | **$0** |
| **Tax on Foreign Income** | 15-48% | **0%** |
| **Path to Citizenship** | Usually none | **3 years** |
| **Physical Presence** | 183 days/yr | **0 days/yr** |
| **Renewals** | Every 1-2 years | Never (permanent) |
| **Crypto Treatment** | Taxed + CRS/DAC8 reporting | 0% CGT, no reporting |
| **Total Cost** | $3K-5K + ongoing taxes | $2,900+ one-time |
| **Risk of Rule Changes** | High (programs get cancelled) | Low (standard immigration) |

## How Paraguay's Residency Works for Remote Workers

You don't need a special "digital nomad" category because Paraguay's standard permanent residency is designed for people like you.

### The Process

1. **Document Preparation** — Apostilled birth certificate, background check, and marriage/power of attorney documents. Your Paraguayan lawyer handles everything.

2. **Entry** — Fly into Asunción. Show your documents. The migration office registers your application.

3. **Cédula** — Within 60-90 days, you receive your Paraguayan cédula (national ID card). This is your permanent residency document.

4. **Done.** No renewals. No income reporting. No tax filings on foreign income. No ongoing obligations beyond one visit every three years to renew your physical cédula.

### What Remote Workers Need

- Passport from most countries (US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, etc.)
- Clean criminal record
- Birth certificate (apostilled)
- Proof of sufficient funds (savings, not income)
- A Paraguayan lawyer to handle the process

**No employer letter. No freelance contracts. No income minimum. No tax returns.**

## Why This Matters More in 2026

The digital nomad space is getting more regulated, not less. In 2026:

- **EU DAC8 goes live** — 49 million European crypto holders face automated exchange of crypto transaction data. Paraguay doesn't participate in DAC8 or CRS.

- **DNV programs getting stricter** — Spain increased enforcement. Portugal is debating income thresholds. Greece added more documentation requirements.

- **Tax authorities cracking down** — Home countries are closing loopholes. Physical presence requirements in DNVs make it easier for your home country to claim you never really left.

Paraguay's approach solves all of this: you have permanent residency (proving you genuinely relocated), zero tax on foreign income, zero reporting, and zero physical presence requirements.

## The "But What About..." Questions

### "Don't I need to live there?"

No. Permanent residency requires one visit every three years to renew your cédula. You can live anywhere in the world.

### "Is it really 0% tax?"

Yes. Paraguay taxes only Paraguay-sourced income. Your remote work for a foreign company, freelance income from foreign clients, crypto gains on foreign exchanges, and passive income from foreign sources are all at 0%.

### "Can I really get citizenship in 3 years?"

Yes. After 3 years of permanent residency, you can apply for naturalization. You need basic Spanish (conversational level), knowledge of Paraguayan civics, and a clean record.

### "What about healthcare?"

Paraguay has both public and private healthcare. Private insurance costs $50-150/month for comprehensive coverage. Asunción has excellent private hospitals.

### "Is it safe?"

Asunción has urban crime like any city of 3 million. Take normal precautions. The expat communities in Asunción's nicer neighborhoods (Villa Morra, Carmelitas) are very safe. The countryside is extremely safe.

## The DNV Comparison: Paraguay Wins Every Category

| Category | Any DNV | Paraguay |
|----------|---------|----------|
| Security | Temporary, uncertain | Permanent, certain |
| Tax savings | 24-48% tax | 0% tax |
| Freedom | 183 days/yr trapped | Travel freely |
| Future | No citizenship path | Passport in 3 years |
| Cost | Losing 24%+ of income | $2,900 one-time |
| Crypto | Reported to home country | Private, untaxed |

## The Bottom Line

Digital nomad visas are a solution to a problem that doesn't exist in Paraguay. Why settle for a temporary visa with income requirements and tax obligations when you can get permanent residency with none of the above?

Paraguay doesn't have a digital nomad visa because it doesn't need one. It offers something better: a real, permanent, tax-free home with a path to citizenship.

The DNV is a trap. Permanent residency in Paraguay is a foundation.

---

*Disclaimer: This article is for informational purposes only. Consult with a qualified immigration lawyer before making any residency decisions.*
