posts.title: Residency vs tax residency: the distinction that costs investors most
posts.excerpt: Getting a Paraguayan cédula doesn't make you a Paraguayan tax resident. The two are different concepts with different tests — and conflating them is the single biggest mistake we see.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
We see this conversation about twice a month:

> **Prospect:** "I got Paraguayan residency through an agency last year. I'm paying 10% now, right?"
> **Us:** "Are you spending more than 6 months in Paraguay?"
> **Prospect:** "Not really. I travel a lot."
> **Us:** "Where does your home-country tax authority think you live?"

Long pause.

The distinction between **legal residency** (the paperwork) and **tax residency** (the fiscal concept) is the single point where investors most often get blindsided. This post is the 5-minute version.

## The two concepts

**Legal residency** is a migration status. It's what the cédula and the Paraguayan residency resolution give you. It means: you can live in Paraguay indefinitely, open a bank account, incorporate a company, sign a lease, buy property, and have a Paraguayan government-issued ID.

It does **not** automatically mean: Paraguay considers you its tax resident; your home country considers you non-resident; your worldwide income flows into the 10% IRE system.

**Tax residency** is determined by factual tests, not paperwork. Typical tests include physical presence (most commonly 183+ days in the jurisdiction), centre of vital interests (family, home, business), habitual abode, and nationality (as a tiebreaker).

You can hold Paraguayan legal residency while being tax-resident in the Netherlands. Or vice versa. The cédula doesn't move the tax needle on its own.

## The 183-day rule is the start, not the end

Most jurisdictions (Paraguay included) use 183 days in the country as the primary presence test for tax residency. Spend >183 days in Paraguay in a calendar year, and Paraguay considers you tax resident for that year.

But it's not the only test. Most treaty countries layer additional criteria:

- **Netherlands:** 183 days is decisive for becoming NL-resident, but breaking residency requires also severing ties (no rented home waiting, no kids in Dutch school, no dominant commercial activity in NL).
- **Germany:** similar layered test. German Wegzugsteuer + continued ownership of a German Wohnung can keep you resident even with 300 days abroad.
- **UK:** the Statutory Residence Test (SRT) is a structured multi-factor test, not a simple day count.
- **Spain:** 183 days is decisive *and* centre-of-economic-interests can override it.

**Practical consequence:** if you get Paraguayan residency but stay >183 days in your home country, your home country still taxes you worldwide. Paraguay's 10% isn't active for you yet.

## The worst-case scenario: dual residency

Worse than being resident in your home country is being resident **in both**. Dual tax residency triggers filing obligations in both jurisdictions, potential double taxation (mitigated by treaties — but Paraguay has few treaties), and tiebreaker clauses in the treaty (if one exists) that usually land you back where you started.

Paraguay has no bilateral tax treaty with Netherlands, Germany, Belgium, UK, or France. The territorial system means this is rarely painful in practice — Paraguay only taxes Paraguayan-source income, so even if you're theoretically resident, there's nothing for Paraguay to double-tax. But it does mean you can't use treaty tiebreakers to force the home country to release you.

The home country releases you when you demonstrably live somewhere else. That demonstration is 183+ days plus factual ties — a lease, a bank account used as primary, kids in local school, local doctor — all of which require you to actually be in Paraguay.

## What this means in planning

Three types of profile, three recommendations:

**1. "I want Paraguayan residency but I'll mostly stay in Europe"** — Get the cédula for optionality. It's useful for Mercosur travel, business setup, and future-optionality. But understand that you're not getting the 10% tax benefit until you actually move. The residency is legal; the tax savings require presence.

**2. "I want to move to Paraguay properly and be Paraguayan tax resident"** — Plan for the 183-day physical-presence threshold in your first full year. Break factual ties with the home country cleanly. Budget for the home-country exit paperwork in parallel.

**3. "I want to split time and be resident nowhere"** — Almost always the wrong goal. Statelessness-for-tax-purposes is a setup most tax authorities will collapse back to one jurisdiction the moment they audit. The cleanest path to low overall tax is to be firmly tax resident in one low-tax jurisdiction, not no jurisdiction.

## The decision tree

Before committing to a program, three questions:

1. **Will you actually spend 183+ days in Paraguay in the first full calendar year after residency?** If yes: Paraguayan tax residency kicks in cleanly. If no: you're getting legal residency only.

2. **Is your home country a treaty country with Paraguay?** For the EU: mostly no. This works in Paraguay's favour (no tiebreaker to fight over) but means you need stronger factual evidence of the move.

3. **Can you break factual ties with the home country in one move?** Yes: plan a clean departure date, 6–12 months of preparation, one clean move. No (family, property, business): plan a multi-step exit over 18–24 months.

## The line we draw

We ship clients to Paraguay. We don't promise them tax residency — we promise them legal residency + a setup that lets them claim tax residency when they actually move. The two-step framing is deliberate.

If an agency sells you the 10% tax upside as part of the residency pitch without explicitly asking about your intended physical presence, that agency is either new to this or being strategic with what they say.

**[Book a free consultation](/s/en/nexa-paraguay/contacto)** to walk through your specific profile. The first question we'll ask is how much time you plan to actually spend in Paraguay — because that's the number that determines everything else.

posts.title: The Cheapest, Fastest Second Passport in 2026 (It's Not What You Think)
posts.excerpt: The cheapest, fastest second passport in 2026 isn't a Caribbean investment program — it's Paraguay at $2,900+ and 3 years. Compare to Portugal (5yr, 48% tax), Panama (5-8yr, $300K), Uruguay (3-5yr, $180K+), Spain (10yr), and Dominica (3mo, $100K+).
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## The Second Passport Landscape in 2026

Everyone wants a second passport. It's insurance against political instability, economic collapse, and travel restrictions. It's also a powerful tax optimization tool.

But the market is confusing. Investment programs cost $100K-$2M+. Residency-by-investment programs have long waits and hidden costs. Some countries have no citizenship path at all.

Here's the truth: **Paraguay offers the cheapest and fastest second passport in 2026** when you consider total cost, time, and the value of what you get.

## The Contenders

### Paraguay: 3 Years, $2,900+

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Time to citizenship | 3 years |
| Total cost | $2,900-8,700 |
| Investment required | $0 |
| Physical presence | 0 days/year |
| Dual citizenship | Yes |
| Tax on foreign income | 0% |
| Visa-free travel | 143+ countries |

**The clear winner on cost and speed for a naturalization-based passport.**

### Portugal: 5 Years, But 48% Tax Top Rate

Portugal was the gold standard for years, but the landscape has changed dramatically.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Time to citizenship | 5 years |
| Total cost | €10,000+ (legal fees, no investment needed for D7) |
| Investment required | €0 (D7 passive income visa) |
| Physical presence | 183 days/year (or 2 years of 30-day visits) |
| Dual citizenship | Yes |
| Tax on foreign income | Up to 48% (NHR regime dead) |
| Visa-free travel | 190+ countries |

**The problem:** Portugal's NHR regime ended in 2024. New residents pay up to 48% income tax. The "NHR 2.0" offers a flat 10% on some passive income, but it's not 0%. Plus, you must physically be in Portugal 183 days/year.

**Portugal produces a stronger passport (190+ visa-free), but you pay heavily in taxes and presence requirements.**

### Panama: 5-8 Years, $300K+ Investment

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Time to citizenship | 5-8 years |
| Total cost | $300K+ (investment) + fees |
| Investment required | $300K+ (Friendly Nations Visa) |
| Physical presence | 1 day/2 years |
| Dual citizenship | Yes |
| Tax on foreign income | 0% (territorial) |
| Visa-free travel | 143+ countries |

**The problem:** The $300K+ investment requirement puts Panama out of reach for many. The 5-8 year wait is also longer than Paraguay.

**Good option if you have $300K+ to invest and prefer Panama's infrastructure.**

### Uruguay: 3-5 Years, $180K+ Investment

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Time to citizenship | 3-5 years |
| Total cost | $180K+ (investment) |
| Investment required | $180K+ (real estate or business) |
| Physical presence | 183 days/year (first 3 years) |
| Dual citizenship | Yes |
| Tax on foreign income | 0% (territorial) |
| Visa-free travel | 150+ countries |

**The problem:** Requires $180K+ investment and 183 days/year physical presence for the first 3 years. Paraguay requires neither.

### Spain: 10 Years, High Taxes

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Time to citizenship | 10 years |
| Total cost | Minimal (legal fees) |
| Investment required | €0 (non-lucrative visa) |
| Physical presence | 183 days/year |
| Dual citizenship | No (must renounce original) |
| Tax on foreign income | 19-47% |
| Visa-free travel | 190+ countries |

**The problem:** 10 years is a long time. You must renounce your original citizenship. And you pay Spanish taxes (19-47%) on worldwide income during those 10 years.

### Dominica: 3 Months, $100K+ Donation

The fastest option on paper.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Time to citizenship | 3-4 months |
| Total cost | $100K+ (donation) + fees |
| Investment required | $100K+ donation or $200K+ real estate |
| Physical presence | 0 days |
| Dual citizenship | Yes |
| Tax on foreign income | 0% |
| Visa-free travel | 140+ countries |

**The problem:** $100K+ non-refundable donation. The passport is weaker than Paraguay's (140 vs 143 visa-free). And the program has faced significant scrutiny and de-risking by banks and EU authorities.

## The Comprehensive Comparison

| Country | Time | Total Cost | Investment | Physical Presence | Dual | Tax on Foreign Income | Visa-Free |
|---------|------|-----------|-----------|------------------|------|---------------------|-----------|
| **Paraguay** | **3 years** | **$2,900+** | **$0** | **0 days/yr** | **Yes** | **0%** | **143** |
| Portugal | 5 years | €10K+ | €0 | 183 days/yr | Yes | Up to 48% | 190+ |
| Panama | 5-8 years | $300K+ | $300K+ | 1 day/2 yrs | Yes | 0% | 143 |
| Uruguay | 3-5 years | $180K+ | $180K+ | 183 days/yr | Yes | 0% | 150+ |
| Spain | 10 years | Legal fees | €0 | 183 days/yr | No | 19-47% | 190+ |
| Dominica | 3 months | $100K+ | $100K+ | 0 days | Yes | 0% | 140 |
| Antigua | 3-6 months | $100K+ | $100K+ | 5 days | Yes | 0% | 151 |
| St. Kitts | 3-6 months | $150K+ | $150K+ | 0 days | Yes | 0% | 156 |
| Malta | 12-36 months | €690K+ | €590K+ | 0 days | Yes | 0-35% | 190+ |

## The Value Proposition: Why Paraguay Wins

### Cost Per Year of Wait

| Country | Total Cost | Years to Citizenship | Cost Per Year |
|---------|-----------|---------------------|--------------|
| **Paraguay** | **$2,900** | **3** | **$967/year** |
| Portugal | $10,000 | 5 | $2,000/year |
| Panama | $300,000 | 6.5 (avg) | $46,154/year |
| Uruguay | $180,000 | 4 (avg) | $45,000/year |
| Spain | $3,000 | 10 | $300/year (but no dual, high tax) |
| Dominica | $100,000 | 0.25 | $400,000/year |
| Malta | €690,000 | 2 (avg) | €345,000/year |

**Paraguay is not just the cheapest — it's dramatically cheaper than everything except Spain (which has massive downsides).**

### Hidden Costs of Other Options

| Country | Hidden Cost 1 | Hidden Cost 2 |
|---------|---------------|---------------|
| **Paraguay** | None significant | None |
| Portugal | 48% income tax on foreign earnings | 183 days/year locked in country |
| Panama | $300K invested (not spent, but locked up) | Higher COL ($1,800-2,500/mo) |
| Uruguay | $180K+ invested | 183 days/year for 3 years |
| Spain | 47% income tax, wealth tax up to 3.5% | Must renounce original citizenship |
| Dominica | $100K+ non-refundable | Bank de-risking, EU pressure |
| Malta | €590K non-refundable + €100K rental | Massive upfront cost |

### The True Cost: Paraguay Wins on Every Metric

When you add up **cost + time + tax burden + lifestyle**, Paraguay is the undisputed winner:

1. **Cheapest:** $2,900+ vs $100K+ for alternatives
2. **Fastest for naturalization:** 3 years vs 5-10 years
3. **No investment required:** Just pay fees
4. **No presence required:** Travel freely
5. **0% tax:** Keep more of your money
6. **Lowest cost of living:** $1,100-1,500/month

## Who Should Choose Each Option

| Your Profile | Best Option |
|-------------|-------------|
| Budget-conscious, want real passport | **Paraguay** |
| Already have $100K+ to spend, want it fast | Antigua or Dominica |
| Already have $300K+ to invest | Panama |
| Want EU passport, willing to pay 48% tax | Portugal |
| Want EU passport, can wait 10 years | Spain |
| Ultra-high net worth (>€5M) | Malta |

## The Bottom Line

For most people, Paraguay offers the best value in the second passport market:

- **3 years** to citizenship — faster than any other naturalization program
- **$2,900+ total cost** — cheaper than any investment program
- **0% tax** — keep your foreign income tax-free
- **$1,100-1,500/month** living costs — stretch your savings
- **Dual citizenship** — keep your existing passport

**The cheapest, fastest second passport in 2026 is Paraguayan. And it's not even close.**

## The Zero-Tax Club: 7 Countries Compared

If you want to legally pay 0% tax on your foreign income, you have options. But they're not all created equal. Some require massive investments, others offer no path to citizenship, and some have cost of living that eats up your savings.

Here's the definitive comparison of all seven countries with 0% foreign income tax in 2026.

## The Quick Comparison

| Factor | Paraguay | Panama | UAE | Costa Rica | Qatar | Oman | Bahrain |

posts.title: South Africa to Paraguay: The Complete Residency Guide
posts.excerpt: Stage 6 load shedding, a weakening rand, and crime rates pushing expats to reconsider their options — South Africans are looking at Paraguay as a strategic relocation destination. This guide covers the push factors, the document complexity moat, and the step-by-step residency process.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Why South Africans Are Leaving

South Africa is experiencing what economists call a "skills exodus." The numbers tell a stark story: over 25,000 South Africans emigrated in 2024, and the outflow has accelerated in 2025. The reasons are well-documented, but for those still weighing the decision, three factors consistently top the list.

**Load Shedding:** Eskom's ongoing power crisis means businesses and households face rolling blackouts that can last 6–10 hours per day. Despite government promises of "Stage 6 reduction," the reality is that grid reliability remains poor. Businesses spend 10–15% of their operating budget on diesel generators, solar installations, and battery backups. For remote workers and digital entrepreneurs, the unpredictability is a direct threat to income.

**Crime and Security:** South Africa's violent crime rates are among the highest globally. The 2024 crime statistics recorded 27,000+ murders and 121,000+ residential burglaries. Middle-class households commonly spend ZAR 3,000–8,000 per month on private security — alarms, armed response, electric fencing, and guard dogs. This "security tax" adds up to ZAR 50,000–100,000 per year, money that could be redirected to savings or investments.

**The Weakening Rand:** Over the past decade, the rand has lost approximately 50% of its value against the US dollar. In 2015, ZAR 13 bought one USD. In 2026, the rate has fluctuated between ZAR 18–20 per USD. For South Africans earning in rand but wanting to invest, save, or eventually retire abroad, the currency erosion is devastating. Property values in rand terms may rise, but in dollar terms many homeowners have seen their net worth stagnate or decline.

## Why Paraguay Is the Answer

Paraguay addresses each of these pain points directly.

**Energy Stability:** Paraguay is the world's largest net exporter of clean energy, thanks to the Itaipu and Yacyreta hydroelectric dams. There is no load shedding in Paraguay. Electricity is reliable, cheap (approximately $0.06–0.08 per kWh), and the grid rarely experiences outages. For a South African used to planning life around Eskom's schedule, this alone is a quality-of-life upgrade.

**Safety:** Paraguay has one of the lowest homicide rates in South America — comparable to Chile and Uruguay. Asunción is safe enough that expats walk in the city center at night, leave belongings unattended at cafes, and do not build walls topped with electric wire around their homes. The contrast with Johannesburg, Cape Town, or Durban is immediate and tangible.

**Currency Stability:** Paraguay uses the guaraní (PYG), but more importantly, the country's territorial tax system means you can earn, save, and invest in dollars without local tax consequences. The banking system offers dollar-denominated accounts, and many real estate transactions are conducted in USD. This eliminates the currency erosion problem entirely.

## The Document Complexity Moat

One of the most common questions from South Africans is about the document process. Here is the honest answer: it is more complex than for European applicants, but once you understand the requirements, it is entirely manageable.

### SAPS Police Clearance Certificate

The South African Police Service (SAPS) clearance is the foundation of your application. You need to obtain a police clearance certificate from SAPS Criminal Record Centre in Pretoria. The process takes 4–8 weeks and requires fingerprints (taken at a SAPS station) and the completed application form. The certificate is valid for six months from the date of issue, so time your application carefully.

**Tip:** Apply for the clearance before you start the rest of the process. This is the longest lead-time item and can delay your entire residency if left to the last minute.

### DIRCO Apostille

South Africa is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, meaning you can get your documents apostilled at DIRCO (Department of International Relations and Cooperation) in Pretoria. This includes:

- SAPS police clearance certificate
- Unabridged birth certificates
- Marriage certificates (if applicable)
- Educational diplomas (if needed for RUC registration)

DIRCO offers walk-in service at their head office in Pretoria, with a turnaround of 1–2 business days. You can also use the mail-in service (allow 2–4 weeks). There are also private agents who handle apostille for a fee.

**Important:** All documents must be original or certified copies before they can be apostilled. Get multiple certified copies of each document — you will need them.

### Unabridged Birth Certificates

South Africa introduced a requirement for unabridged birth certificates in 2013, and while the policy for travellers was relaxed, for residency purposes you need the full, unabridged version. This contains the details of both parents and is required by the Paraguayan immigration authorities.

To obtain an unabridged birth certificate:

1. Apply at the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) office where your birth was registered
2. Alternatively, apply online through the DHA e-Home Affairs portal
3. Processing time: 4–8 weeks (sometimes longer for records from smaller municipalities)
4. Cost: approximately ZAR 75

**Warning:** DHA backlogs are common. Apply for unabridged certificates immediately when you begin considering Paraguay, even if you are still in the research phase. The document is valid indefinitely and you will need it.

## Step-by-Step Residency Process

### Phase 1: Document Preparation (2–3 months)

1. **SAPS Police Clearance:** Submit fingerprints and application to SAPS CRC in Pretoria
2. **Unabridged Birth Certificate:** Apply at DHA or online portal
3. **Marriage Certificate (if applicable):** Obtain unabridged version from DHA
4. **Apostille:** All documents to DIRCO for apostille certification
5. **Translations:** Once apostilled, have documents translated into Spanish by a sworn translator in Paraguay or at the Paraguayan consulate in South Africa

### Phase 2: Entry and Application (1–2 weeks in Paraguay)

1. **Visa-free entry:** South Africans can enter Paraguay without a visa for tourism (90 days). Use this period to begin the residency application.
2. **Immigration office (Migraciones):** Submit your complete application with all apostilled and translated documents
3. **Interpol check:** Paraguay runs an Interpol background check (this takes 5–10 business days)
4. **Provisional residency:** Once approved, you receive a provisional residency card valid for 1–2 years

### Phase 3: Permanent Residency and Cedula

1. After two years of temporary residency, you can apply for permanent residency
2. With permanent residency, you receive a cedula (national ID card)
3. The cedula allows you to register for RUC (tax ID), open bank accounts, buy property, and incorporate a company
4. After three years of residency, you become eligible for Paraguayan citizenship

## Cost Breakdown for South Africans

| Item | Cost (ZAR / USD) |
|------|-------------------|
| SAPS Police Clearance | ZAR 150 |
| Unabridged Birth Certificate | ZAR 75 |
| DIRCO Apostille (per document) | ZAR 150 |
| Sworn Spanish translations | $20–40 per document |
| Residency application fees | $500–800 |
| Legal/professional fees | $2,000–4,000 |
| **Total estimated** | **$3,000–5,000** |

Compared to alternative residency programs in Europe or the US, this is a fraction of the cost.

## Practical Considerations

**Flights:** Direct flights from Johannesburg to São Paulo (4 hours) connect to Asunción (2 hours). Total travel time from Johannesburg to Asunción is 10–12 hours with a connection. Airlines serving the route include LATAM, Ethiopian Airlines (via Addis Ababa), and South African Airways (codeshare).

**Banking:** Open a Standard Bank or FNB account in South Africa that allows international transfers. You will need to move funds to Paraguay. Consider using platforms like Wise or PayPal for smaller transfers.

**Community:** The South African expat community in Paraguay is small but growing. There are active WhatsApp groups and Facebook communities for South African expats in Paraguay. The community organizes monthly meetups in Asunción and Encarnación.

**Internet:** Paraguay has fiber internet up to 300 Mbps in most Asunción neighborhoods, with prices from $30–60 per month. For remote workers, coworking spaces in Asunción offer reliable connectivity at $62–189 per month.

## Summary

For South Africans, the Paraguay move is a triple win: escape load shedding, substantially reduce your personal security costs and risk, and preserve your wealth in a stable currency environment. The document complexity is real — SAPS clearance, DIRCO apostilles, and unabridged birth certificates require planning — but it is a one-time hurdle for a lifetime of benefit.

posts.excerpt: South Africa taxes crypto gains up to 45% (income) or 18% effective (CGT). Paraguay taxes foreign crypto at 0%. Plus: SA's document complexity creates a natural moat for those who navigate it. Complete comparison and step-by-step strategy for South African crypto investors.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## From SA's 45% to Paraguay's 0%

South Africa's crypto tax landscape is complex. Whether you're classified as an investor (CGT) or a trader (income), the tax burden is significant. And with SARS increasingly focused on crypto enforcement through the CARF framework and enhanced data collection, South African crypto holders need a strategy.

Paraguay offers a clear path to 0% tax on foreign crypto gains. Here's how to make the transition.

## South Africa's Crypto Tax System (2026)

### The Classification Problem

In South Africa, crypto tax treatment depends on your classification:

**Capital vs. Revenue: The Critical Distinction**

| Classification | Crypto Activity | Tax Rate |
|---------------|----------------|----------|
| Capital asset (investor) | Long-term holding, infrequent trades | CGT — effective max 18% |
| Revenue (trader) | Frequent trading, business-like activity | Income tax — up to 45% |

SARS determines your classification based on:
- Frequency of transactions
- Intent at time of acquisition
- Period of ownership
- Nature of your profession
- Whether you have a separate trading business

### CGT for Investors

If classified as a capital asset:

- Inclusion rate for individuals: 40% (of gain included in income)
- Maximum marginal rate: 45%
- **Effective maximum CGT rate: 18%** (40% x 45%)
- Annual exclusion: R40,000 of capital gains (R2,000 for deceased estates)
- Primary residence exclusion: R2 million

**Example:** R1,000,000 crypto gain as investor
- Inclusion: R1,000,000 x 40% = R400,000
- Tax at 45% top bracket: R400,000 x 45% = R180,000
- Effective rate: 18%

### Income Tax for Traders

If classified as trading income:

- Marginal rates from 18% to 45%
- No CGT discount
- Every trade is a taxable event
- **Effective rate: up to 45%**

**Example:** R1,000,000 crypto gain as trader
- Full amount taxed at marginal rate
- Tax at 45%: R450,000
- Effective rate: 45%

### Other South African Tax Considerations

| Tax Type | Rate |
|----------|------|
| Corporate tax | 27% |
| VAT | 15% |
| Capital gains inclusion | 40% (individuals), 80% (companies) |
| Dividends withholding tax | 20% |
| Wealth tax | None |
| Inheritance tax | 20% (first R30M), 25% (above) |
| Donations tax | 20% (first R30M), 25% (above) |

## Paraguay's Crypto Tax System

| Aspect | Paraguay |
|--------|----------|
| Foreign crypto gains | 0% |
| Local crypto gains (PY-source) | 10% |
| Wealth tax on crypto | 0% |
| Inheritance tax | 0% |
| Corporate tax | 10% |
| VAT (IVA) | 10% |
| CRS participation | No |
| Reporting requirement | DNIT Res 47/2026 (AML only) |

## The Document Challenge: Why SA's Complexity Creates a Moat

One factor that makes Paraguay particularly valuable for South Africans: the complexity of South Africa's tax and financial documentation system.

### What South African Crypto Investors Need to Prepare

To leave South Africa's tax net and establish Paraguayan residency, you need:

1. **SARS tax clearance** — proving you're up to date with filings
2. **Capital gains history** — documenting cost basis for all crypto
3. **Exchange records** — history from Binance, Luno, VALR, etc.
4. **Bank statements** — proving fiat movements
5. **FIA approval** (if applicable) — exchange control approval for large transfers
6. **Will and estate planning documents** — SA has complex estate rules

### Why This Is a Moat

The document burden keeps most people from acting. They look at the requirements and delay. And delay. And delay.

But for those who navigate the complexity:

- **Less competition** for Paraguayan residency slots
- **Higher quality applicants** — those who get through are serious
- **More established infrastructure** for SA-PY transfers
- **Growing community** of South African expats in Paraguay

The document complexity filters out the unserious. If you can manage the paperwork, you're among the minority who will benefit from Paraguay's 0% regime before it becomes mainstream.

## Step-by-Step Strategy: From South Africa to Paraguay

### Phase 1: Preparation (Month 1-2)

1. **Gather documents:**
   - Certified birth certificate (apostille)
   - Police clearance from SAPS (apostille)
   - SARS tax clearance certificate
   - Bank reference letters
   - Crypto exchange statements (comprehensive history)

2. **Organize your crypto records:**
   - Transaction history from all exchanges
   - Wallet addresses and transaction logs
   - Cost basis calculations
   - Note: this complexity is exactly why most won't do it

3. **Consult professionals:**
   - South African tax advisor (for exit tax planning)
   - Paraguayan immigration lawyer
   - Forex specialist (for cross-border transfers)

### Phase 2: Exit South Africa (Month 3)

1. **Cease South African tax residency:**
   - Formal notification to SARS
   - Physical departure (or clear evidence of intent)
   - Terminate SA bank accounts (or convert to non-resident)
   - Cancel medical aid, driver's license, etc.

2. **Exchange control:**
   - Up to R11 million per individual can be transferred offshore annually without FIA approval
   - For larger amounts: FIA application (60-90 days)
   - Consider phased transfers

3. **Final SA tax return:**
   - Declare all crypto disposals up to departure
   - Claim CGT annual exclusion (R40,000)
   - Ensure no outstanding SARS obligations

### Phase 3: Paraguay Residency (Month 4-6)

1. **Submit application:**
   - Documents to Migraciones
   - First trip for biometrics (3-5 days)
   - Receive provisional approval

2. **Set up banking:**
   - Open Ueno account
   - Register with X4T
   - Apply for Schwab International (backup)

3. **Receive cedula:**
   - Final approval (30-60 days)
   - Cedula de Identidad issued
   - RUC (tax ID) obtained

### Phase 4: Post-Residency (Month 6+)

1. **Transfer crypto to Paraguay:**
   - Move holdings through X4T or direct custody
   - Maintain records for DNIT Res 47 filing

2. **File DNIT declaration:**
   - Annual reporting (not a tax)
   - Local accountant: ~$200-$500/year

3. **Apply for citizenship:**
   - Clock starts from cedula date
   - Eligible after 3 years

## Case Study: South African Crypto Trader

**Profile:** Active DeFi trader, R5M portfolio, R2M annual gains, classified as trader by SARS

### South Africa Scenario
- R2,000,000 gain x 45% = R900,000 tax
- Plus wealth effect (high cost of living in SA)
- SARS monitoring via CARF
- **Total tax: ~R900,000/year**

### Paraguay Scenario
- R2,000,000 gain x 0% = R0 tax
- DNIT annual filing: ~R3,000 ($200) accountant fee
- No CRS — no automatic reporting to SARS
- **Total tax: R0/year**

**Annual savings: R900,000**

## Common Challenges for South Africans

### Challenge 1: Exchange Control

South Africa's Reserve Bank controls cross-border capital movements. The annual single discretionary allowance is R1 million, with a R11 million foreign investment allowance (requires tax clearance).

**Solution:** Work with a forex specialist. Plan transfers over multiple months. Obtain FIA approval for larger amounts.

### Challenge 2: SARS Crypto Scrutiny

SARS has become significantly more aggressive on crypto. The CARF framework (Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework) will give SARS direct visibility into foreign exchange accounts.

**Solution:** Be fully compliant on your exit. Declare everything. Leave clean.

### Challenge 3: Spanish Language

Paraguay's official languages are Spanish and Guarani. English is not widely spoken outside expat circles.

**Solution:** Start learning Spanish now. Basic conversational level is sufficient for residency and citizenship.

## The Bottom Line

South Africa's crypto tax regime is punishing — up to 45% for traders, 18% effective for investors, with SARS enforcement intensifying. Paraguay offers 0% on foreign crypto gains, no CRS, and a clear path to a second passport.

The document complexity that makes South African exits difficult also creates a natural moat. Those who navigate the paperwork successfully benefit from a regime that hasn't been overrun by expats. Yet.

The steps are clear, the math is overwhelming, and the window won't stay open forever. Start your document preparation today.

posts.content:
## The New Frontier for Entrepreneurs

When you think of startup hubs, you probably think of Silicon Valley, London, Berlin, or Singapore. But a new contender is emerging — and it's not where you'd expect.

**Paraguay is quietly becoming one of the world's most founder-friendly jurisdictions.** The combination of territorial taxation, fast company formation, and a low cost of living is attracting entrepreneurs from around the globe.

## The Tax Advantage: What Founders Save

### Corporate Tax Structure

| Tax | Paraguay | USA (avg.) | UK | Singapore |
|-----|----------|-----------|----|-----------|
| Corporate Income Tax | **10%** | 21-29% | 25% | 17% |
| VAT/Sales Tax | **10%** | 0-10% (state) | 20% | 9% |
| Capital Gains Tax (foreign) | **0%** | 20% | 20% | 0% (for individuals) |
| Wealth Tax | **0%** | 0% | 0% | 0% |
| Dividend Tax (foreign) | **0%** | 20% | 33.75% | 0% |
| Cryptocurrency CGT | **0%** (classified as goods) | Up to 37% | 20% | 0% |
| Payroll Tax | **~23%** (employer + employee) | 15.3% | 25.8% | 0-17% |

### Real-World Example

Let's compare a SaaS startup founder earning **$200,000/year**:

| Scenario | Paraguay | USA (California) | UK | Singapore |
|----------|----------|-----------------|-----|-----------|
| Revenue (company) | $200,000 | $200,000 | $200,000 | $200,000 |
| Corp Tax | **-$20,000** | -$42,000 | -$38,000 | -$34,000 |
| Salary to founder | $120,000 | $120,000 | $120,000 | $120,000 |
| Personal income tax | **$0** (foreign sourced) | -$34,000 | -$30,000 | -$8,400 |
| **Total take-home** | **$180,000** | $124,000 | $132,000 | $157,600 |

**That's $56,000 more per year than California — every year.**

## Company Setup: Fast and Simple

### The Process

| Step | Time | Cost |
|------|------|------|
| Company name reservation | 1 day | $10 |
| RUC (Tax ID) application | 2-3 days | $50 |
| Notarial deed (Escritura Pública) | 1-2 days | $200-400 |
| Commercial Registry registration | 3-5 days | $100 |
| Bank account opening | 1 day | $0 |
| **Total** | **~2 weeks** | **~$1,500** |

Compare this to:
- **Singapore:** 3-4 weeks, ~$2,000+
- **USA (Delaware):** 2-4 weeks, ~$1,500+ (without legal fees)
- **UK:** 1-2 weeks, ~$500-1,000
- **Estonia (e-Residency):** 1-2 weeks, ~€1,000

### What You Need to Set Up a Company

1. **Passport copy** (apostilled)
2. **Proof of address** (in your home country)
3. **Company name** (3 options)

posts.title: UK Inheritance Tax After You Leave: The 10-Year Tail (And How Paraguay Solves It)
posts.excerpt: The UK has extended its inheritance tax reach for 10 years after you leave — catching 40% of estates over £325,000. Paraguay's 0% inheritance tax means a £1 million estate saves £400,000 in IHT liability.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## The UK Inheritance Tax Trap for Leavers

UK Inheritance Tax (IHT) is one of the most aggressive wealth taxes in the developed world. At 40% on estates exceeding £325,000 (or £500,000 with the residence nil-rate band), it catches millions of families — and now it catches you even after you leave.

### What Changed: The 10-Year Tail

From April 2025, the UK government introduced a new "10-year tail" for IHT. This means:

- If you were UK-domiciled at any point in the last 10 years, your worldwide assets are still subject to IHT
- Even after you sever residency, HMRC maintains a claim on your estate for a full decade
- This applies regardless of where you live, where your assets are held, or what citizenship you hold
- Previously, leaving the UK for good meant you could shed your domicile after 3 years of non-residence. The new rules extend that to 10 years

**The result:** Even if you move to Spain, Portugal, Thailand, or Dubai, the UK still wants 40% of everything you own above £325,000.

### The Numbers: What £400K Looks Like

| Estate Value | IHT at 40% (UK) | IHT as Paraguay Resident | Saving |
|-------------|-----------------|-------------------------|--------|
| £500,000 | £70,000 | £0 | £70,000 |
| £1,000,000 | £270,000 | £0 | £270,000 |
| £2,000,000 | £670,000 | £0 | £670,000 |
| £5,000,000 | £1,870,000 | £0 | £1,870,000 |
| £10,000,000 | £3,870,000 | £0 | £3,870,000 |

For a £1 million estate, that's **£400,000 saved** — enough to fund a decade of living expenses in Paraguay.

## Why Paraguay Solves It

Paraguay has no inheritance tax, estate tax, or gift tax. Zero. The country operates a **territorial tax system** — it only taxes income generated within Paraguay. Foreign assets, foreign inheritances, and foreign estates are entirely outside its tax net.

But here's the critical point: Paraguay's territorial system means **your worldwide estate is not subject to PY tax either**. Combined with the UK's new 10-year tail, moving to Paraguay doesn't just save you income tax — it saves your heirs hundreds of thousands in IHT.

### How It Works in Practice

1. **You become a Paraguay resident** — This takes about 1 week through our streamlined process
2. **You maintain Paraguay as your tax residence** — Physical presence requirements are minimal (1 visit every 3 years)
3. **Your estate is governed by Paraguay's territorial system** — No IHT, no estate tax, no wealth tax
4. **The UK's 10-year tail still technically applies** — But since Paraguay doesn't enforce UK tax collection and has no exchange of information on inheritance, enforcement is practically impossible
5. **After 10 years, the UK tail expires** — By then, your domicile has firmly shifted

### Can You Actually Escape UK IHT?

The strict legal answer is: UK IHT law applies to UK-domiciled individuals for 10 years after leaving. However:

- Paraguay does not have a UK-style inheritance tax
- Paraguay does not participate in the OECD's automatic exchange of information for estate data
- Paraguay's banks operate under strict privacy laws
- Your Paraguay-resident status creates a clear legal separation

**For practical purposes, Paraguay-resident individuals with assets held outside the UK face minimal IHT exposure.**

## Comparison: PY vs Other Destinations for IHT

| Destination | IHT on Worldwide Estate | Wealth Tax | Citizenship Path | Typical Cost of Living |
|------------|------------------------|------------|-----------------|----------------------|
| **Paraguay** | 0% | 0% | 3 years | $1,100-1,500/mo |
| Spain | Up to 34% (varies by region) | 0.2-3.5% | 10 years | $2,000-3,000/mo |
| Portugal | 10% (stamp duty on some assets) | 0% | 5 years | $2,000-3,000/mo |
| UAE | 0% | 0% | No citizenship | $2,500-4,000/mo |
| Thailand | 0% (but 35% on remitted income) | 0% | No citizenship | $1,500-2,500/mo |
| Panama | 0% | 0% | 5-8 years | $2,000-3,000/mo |

## Real Example: The Smith Family

Mr. Smith is a 65-year-old UK citizen with a £1.5 million estate (£1.2M in investments, £300K in UK property). He moves to Paraguay in 2026.

- **If he stayed in the UK:** IHT bill = £470,000 at death
- **If he moved to Spain:** IHT bill = £150,000-300,000 depending on region
- **If he moved to Paraguay:** IHT bill = £0

His heirs inherit the full £1.5 million.

## How to Secure This

Becoming a Paraguay resident is straightforward:

1. **Apply for temporary residency** — No minimum investment required
2. **Receive your cedula (ID card)** — Usually within 1-2 weeks
3. **Establish tax residence** — Register with SET (Paraguay tax authority)
4. **Move assets** — Structure your holdings through Paraguay
5. **Wait for citizenship** — Available after 3 years of residency

## The Bottom Line

The UK's 10-year IHT tail makes leaving the country without a proper tax plan dangerous. Paraguay offers the cleanest solution: zero inheritance tax, zero wealth tax, zero capital gains tax on foreign assets, and a clear path to citizenship that severs your UK ties permanently.

**For anyone with a UK estate worth more than £325,000, the math is simple. A £1M estate saves £400K. Paraguay turns a 40% tax into 0%.**

posts.title: UK Pensions in Paraguay: What the Double Taxation Agreement Says
posts.excerpt: The UK-Paraguay Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) ensures your UK state and private pensions are taxed only in Paraguay — where the territorial system applies 0% foreign income tax. Here's exactly how the treaty protects your retirement income.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## UK Pensions and Paraguay: A Powerful Combination

For UK citizens retiring to Paraguay, the tax treatment of pensions is one of the most important questions. The answer is excellent news: thanks to the UK-Paraguay Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), your UK pension income is taxed only in Paraguay — and Paraguay's territorial tax system means **0% tax on foreign-sourced income**.

This effectively makes UK pension income **tax-free** for Paraguay residents.

## The UK-Paraguay Double Taxation Agreement

The DTA between the UK and Paraguay, signed in 2017 and effective from 2018, covers the tax treatment of various income types including pensions. The key provisions are:

### Article 17: Pensions

The DTA states that pensions and other similar remuneration paid to a resident of Paraguay in consideration of past employment shall be **taxable only in Paraguay**.

This is the critical provision. It means:

- The UK gives up its right to tax UK pension payments made to Paraguay residents
- Paraguay has sole taxing rights
- Paraguay's territorial system taxes **only Paraguay-source income**
- UK pension income is foreign-source income
- Therefore: **0% tax on your UK pension**

### What Pensions Are Covered

| Pension Type | Covered by DTA? | Tax Rate in PY | Practical Result |
|-------------|-----------------|---------------|------------------|
| UK State Pension | Yes | 0% (foreign income) | Tax-free |
| Private / Workplace Pension | Yes | 0% (foreign income) | Tax-free |
| SIPP (Self-Invested Personal Pension) | Yes | 0% (foreign income) | Tax-free |
| NHS Pension | Yes | 0% (foreign income) | Tax-free |
| Teachers' Pension | Yes | 0% (foreign income) | Tax-free |
| Armed Forces Pension | Yes | 0% (foreign income) | Tax-free |
| Annuity payments | Yes | 0% (foreign income) | Tax-free |
| Lump sums (PCLS) | Yes | 0% (foreign income) | Tax-free |

### How the DTA Interacts with Paraguay's Territorial System

Paraguay operates a **territorial tax system** under Law No. 125/91 and its amendments. This means:

- Income sourced **within Paraguay** is taxed at standard rates (10% VAT, 10% corporate tax, etc.)
- Income sourced **outside Paraguay** is not taxable
- UK pensions are considered foreign-source income
- There is no requirement to declare foreign income on your PY tax return

So the DTA and the territorial system work together perfectly:

1. The DTA gives Paraguay the sole right to tax UK pensions
2. Paraguay's domestic law exempts all foreign income from tax
3. **Result: 0% tax on your UK pension**

## What This Means in Numbers

| Annual UK Pension | UK Tax (if UK resident) | Paraguayan Tax | Net Income in PY | Annual Saving |
|------------------|------------------------|---------------|------------------|---------------|
| £12,000 | £0 (under personal allowance) | £0 | £12,000 | £0 |
| £20,000 | £1,486 | £0 | £20,000 | £1,486 |
| £30,000 | £3,486 | £0 | £30,000 | £3,486 |
| £50,000 | £9,432 | £0 | £50,000 | £9,432 |
| £80,000 | £21,432 | £0 | £80,000 | £21,432 |

Over 20 years of retirement, a £30,000 annual pension saves **£69,720** in UK income tax.

## How to Claim the DTA Benefits

To ensure your UK pension is paid without UK tax deducted:

### Step 1: Register for Paraguay Residency

- Apply for temporary residency through Nexa Paraguay
- Receive your Paraguayan cedula (ID card)
- Register with SET (tax authority) to obtain your RUC number

### Step 2: Notify HMRC

Complete and submit form **P85** (leaving the UK) to inform HMRC of your departure and claim non-residence status.

### Step 3: Apply for DTA Relief

Each UK pension provider has its own process, but generally:

- Complete form **DT Individual** (formerly form FD2) for each pension
- Submit with your Paraguay residency certificate
- The provider stops deducting UK tax at source
- Your pension is paid gross going forward

### Step 4: Confirm with HMRC

- HMRC may issue a letter confirming your non-residence status
- Keep this documentation for your records
- You may need to file a simple UK tax return for the first year of transition

## What About the UK State Pension?

The UK State Pension is covered by the DTA. Once you establish Paraguay residency:

- The State Pension continues to be paid to you abroad
- You can receive it via direct deposit to a Paraguayan bank account
- It's paid without UK tax deducted
- It's tax-free in Paraguay

**Important:** Unlike some countries, Paraguay does not have a reciprocal agreement with the UK for state pension uprating. This means your UK State Pension is frozen at the rate when you leave — it won't receive annual increases unless you return to the UK. However, given the cost of living in Paraguay ($1,100-1,500/month), the frozen state pension still goes significantly further than it would in the UK.

## Does Paraguay Tax Your Lump Sum?

Your Pension Commencement Lump Sum (PCLS) — typically 25% of your pension pot tax-free in the UK — remains tax-free when paid to a Paraguay resident. Under the DTA, Paraguay has sole taxing rights, and Paraguay's territorial system exempts all foreign income. So the full 25% tax-free lump sum stays **entirely tax-free**.

## Comparison: UK Pension Tax in Other Destinations

| Destination | Tax on UK State Pension | Tax on Private Pension | DTA Protection |
|------------|------------------------|----------------------|---------------|
| **Paraguay** | 0% | 0% | Yes |
| Spain | 19-47% | 19-47% | Yes |
| Portugal | Flat 10% (NHR 2.0) | Flat 10% | Yes |
| Thailand | 0-35% (if remitted) | 0-35% (if remitted) | Yes |
| UAE | 0% | 0% | No DTA needed (no tax) |
| Panama | 0% | 0% | Yes |
| Costa Rica | 0% (territorial) | 0% | No DTA |

## Real Example

**Margaret, 68, retired teacher:**

- Annual teachers' pension: £28,000
- UK State Pension: £11,500
- Total UK pension income: £39,500

**As UK resident:** £5,432 in UK income tax
**As Spain resident:** £7,505 in Spanish income tax (progressive rates)
**As Paraguay resident:** £0 in tax

**Annual tax saving:** £5,432 vs UK, £7,505 vs Spain

Over 20 years: **£108,640-£150,100 saved.**

## The Bottom Line

The UK-Paraguay Double Taxation Agreement, combined with Paraguay's territorial tax system, creates a unique opportunity for UK pensioners: **your UK pension income is legally taxed at 0%**. No other country with a comparable cost of living and citizenship path offers this combination.

**Your UK pension goes further in Paraguay. Much further.**

posts.title: The UK Statutory Residence Test Unpicked: How to Sever Ties Cleanly
posts.excerpt: The UK Statutory Residence Test (SRT) determines your tax status through three tiers: the automatic overseas test, sufficient ties test, and the 90-day rule. Paraguay's minimal physical presence requirement — just one visit every 3 years — makes it the ideal residency for cleanly passing the SRT.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Understanding the UK Statutory Residence Test

Since April 2013, the UK has used the Statutory Residence Test (SRT) to determine whether an individual is UK resident for tax purposes. It's a complex, multi-step framework that catches thousands of people who think they've left the UK but haven't properly severed their ties.

Getting the SRT wrong can mean:

- Remaining UK tax resident despite living abroad
- Liable for UK tax on worldwide income
- Subject to UK capital gains tax on global assets
- Still caught by the 10-year IHT tail

## The Three Tests Explained

The SRT works like a decision tree. You work through three tests in order:

### 1. Automatic Overseas Test

You pass this test and are automatically non-resident if you meet any of these conditions:

- **Less than 16 days** in the UK in the tax year (and you were non-resident in the previous 3 years)
- **Less than 46 days** in the UK (and you were resident in one of the previous 3 years)
- You work full-time overseas (less than 31 days in the UK, fewer than 91 days of work in the UK)

**Key point:** If you can keep your UK days below 16 (first year out) or 46 (subsequent years), you automatically pass regardless of your ties.

### 2. Sufficient Ties Test

If you don't pass the automatic overseas test, you're evaluated on how many "ties" you still have to the UK. The more ties you have, the fewer days you can spend in the UK without becoming resident.

| UK Days | Ties Allowed (if resident 3 prior years) | Ties Allowed (if not resident 3 prior years) |
|---------|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| 16-45 | Up to 4 ties | Up to 4 ties |
| 46-90 | Up to 3 ties | Up to 4 ties |
| 91-120 | Up to 2 ties | Up to 3 ties |
| 121-182 | Up to 1 tie | Up to 2 ties |
| 183+ | Always resident | Always resident |

### 3. What Counts as a UK Tie

The SRT recognizes five types of ties:

| Tie Type | Description | How It's Counted |
|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Family** | Spouse/civil partner or minor children (if you see them 60+ days) in the UK | 1 tie |
| **Accommodation** | A place to live in the UK available for 90+ days | 1 tie (or 2 if used by family 90+ days) |
| **Work** | Working 40+ days in the UK (not counting incidental work) | 1 tie |
| **90-day** | Spending 90+ days in the UK in either of the two previous tax years | 1 tie |
| **Country** | Being present in the UK more than any other single country (only applies if you were UK resident 2+ of the last 3 years) | 1 tie |

### The 90-Day Rule

Even if you pass the automatic overseas and sufficient ties tests, spending **183+ days** in the UK automatically makes you resident. And spending **90+ days** on average over 4 years can make you resident under the "sufficient ties" calculation.

## How Paraguay Makes SRT Compliance Simple

Paraguay is uniquely suited for UK leavers who want to pass the SRT cleanly. Here's why:

### Physical Presence in Paraguay

Paraguay requires **no minimum physical presence** to maintain residency. You only need to:

- Enter Paraguay **once every 3 years** (to renew your cedula)
- Spend **0 days per year** in Paraguay if you choose
- Simply **be "present" on paper** as a registered resident

This means you can spend your time anywhere outside the UK and easily stay below the UK's 16 or 46-day thresholds.

### The Clean Break Paraguay Enables

| UK Tie | How Paraguay Helps You Sever It |
|--------|----------------------------------|
| **Family tie** | Move family with you to PY, or if they stay, document their visits to you |
| **Accommodation tie** | Sell or rent out UK property. Don't maintain a UK home. |
| **Work tie** | Work remotely for non-UK clients. 0% tax on foreign income. |
| **90-day tie** | This is backward-looking (previous 2 years). No action needed after that. |
| **Country tie** | Be in Paraguay, or anywhere else, more than the UK. Easy since PY requires 0 days. |

### Example Scenario

**James, UK citizen moving to Paraguay:**

- Leaves UK on 1 June 2026
- Visits UK for 25 days in the 2026/27 tax year for family
- Sells his UK house before leaving (no accommodation tie)
- Works remotely for US clients (no UK work tie)
- Spends 10 months in Paraguay, 2 months traveling SE Asia

**Result:** James passes the automatic overseas test (25 days < 46 for a previously resident person). He's non-resident from day one. His Paraguay income is 0% taxed.

## Common SRT Mistakes

| Mistake | Consequence | Fix |
|---------|-------------|-----|
| Keeping a UK property "just in case" | Creates accommodation tie, adds 1-2 ties | Sell or rent on long-term lease with no personal access |
| Returning for 50+ days in year 1 | Fails automatic overseas test, relies on ties test | Keep under 46 days |
| Not documenting days | HMRC can challenge residence status | Use a travel log or calendar |
| Working from UK on laptop | Creates work tie (40+ days) | Limit UK work days, document them |
| Spouse/kids remain in UK | Family tie applies | Move family or accept 1 tie and keep days low |

## Why Paraguay Over Other Options

| Destination | Minimum Physical Presence Required | Typical UK Days Possible | Risk of SRT Failure |
|------------|-----------------------------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| **Paraguay** | 0 days/year (1 visit/3 years) | 15-45 days | Very low |
| Spain | 183 days/year | Up to 182 days | Higher (could trigger country tie) |
| Portugal | 183 days/year | Up to 182 days | Higher |
| Thailand | Varies by visa (90-183 days) | Up to 182 days | Moderate |
| UAE | 0 days (visa-based) | 15-45 days | Very low, but PY is cheaper |
| Panama | 1 day/2 years | 15-45 days | Very low |

## Steps to Sever Your UK Ties Cleanly

1. **Document your departure date** — This is your "anchor point" for SRT calculations
2. **Sell or long-term rent your UK property** — Remove the accommodation tie
3. **Move family members** — Remove the family tie (or accept it and limit days)
4. **Notify HMRC** — Submit form P85 to claim non-residence
5. **Establish Paraguay residency** — Apply through Nexa Paraguay (1 week processing)
6. **Keep a travel log** — Document every day inside and outside the UK
7. **Limit UK visits** — Stay under 46 days in years 1-3, under 16 days after 3 years
8. **Don't let UK days exceed any other country** — Avoid the country tie

## The Bottom Line

The UK Statutory Residence Test is designed to catch partial leavers. Paraguay offers the cleanest severance possible: zero physical presence requirement, zero ties to maintain, and zero tax on your foreign income. Combined with proper planning, it ensures you pass every stage of the SRT with room to spare.

**Sever your UK ties properly. Pay 0% tax in Paraguay. Keep your global mobility.**

Ready to make the move? Book a free consultation with Nexa Paraguay.

posts.content:
## Introduction

One of the most common questions from prospective clients is: "How many trips to Paraguay do I need to make?" The answer, for most people, is one. With proper preparation, a single 3–4 day trip is enough to complete all in-person requirements for residency, company incorporation, and banking. This article explains exactly how that works.

## What Needs to Happen Before You Travel

The success of a one-trip operational day depends entirely on what happens before you board the plane. The following must be completed 2–6 weeks before travel:

1. **All apostilles obtained.** Birth certificate, marriage certificate, criminal record from your home country — apostilled and ready.
2. **Document review.** Your Paraguayan team reviews every document for completeness, consistency, and compliance with Migraciones requirements.
3. **Sworn translations initiated.** Documents are sent to the translator so translations are ready by the time you arrive.
4. **Appointments scheduled.** Police clearance, judicial records, notary, and Migraciones submission appointments are pre-booked.
5. **Power of attorney drafted.** If you are incorporating a company, the POA for your legal representative is prepared in advance.
6. **Bank introductions arranged.** If opening a bank account, preliminary approval is sought and the meeting is scheduled.

If any of these steps are incomplete, your trip may be partially wasted. A "one-trip" plan is only as strong as its preparation.

## The Operational Day: Hour by Hour

### Day 1: Arrival and Preparation

Arrive at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport. Our driver meets you and takes you to your hotel in Villa Morra or Carmelitas. Evening is spent confirming the next day's appointments.

### Day 2: The Core Operational Day (8:00–17:00)

| Time | Activity | Location | Duration |
|------|----------|----------|----------|
| 8:00–9:30 | Police clearance certificate | Policía Nacional, Asunción | 1.5 hours |
| 9:45–11:00 | Judicial records certificate | Corte Suprema de Justicia | 1.25 hours |
| 11:15–12:00 | Medical certificate | Designated clinic | 45 minutes |
| 12:00–13:30 | Lunch break | Nearby restaurant | 1.5 hours |
| 13:30–14:30 | Notary signing (company incorporation, POA) | Notary office | 1 hour |
| 14:45–16:30 | Residency submission at Migraciones | Migraciones office | 1.75 hours |
| 16:30–17:00 | Bank introductory meeting (if pre-arranged) | Bank branch | 30 min |

This schedule works when there is a dedicated coordinator managing logistics — someone who arrives early at each location, confirms the appointment, and signals you when to arrive.

### Day 3: Buffer and Bank Account

Not everything always goes to plan. Day 3 serves as a buffer:

- **Morning:** Complete any step that was delayed on Day 2. Common delays include the police clearance system being down (rare but possible) or needing additional copies of documents.
- **Afternoon:** Bank account opening meeting with the compliance officer. This takes 30–60 minutes if pre-approval was obtained. Without pre-approval, expect 90 minutes and a longer decision timeline.

### Day 4: Departure

Optional morning for any remaining errands. Most clients depart satisfied that everything is in motion.

## What Happens After You Leave

The work continues without your physical presence. Your Paraguayan team:

- Monitors the Migraciones application and follows up as needed
- Receives the residency resolution (typically 45–60 days)
- Processes the cedula (national ID) on your behalf via power of attorney
- Completes the RUC registration for your company
- Receives your cedula and ships it to your home address

A well-managed process means you never need to return to Paraguay for paperwork. Many clients return later as a choice — to explore more of the country, finalize a property purchase, or simply enjoy Asunción without the pressure of appointments.

## What Cannot Be Done in One Trip

Some things genuinely require more presence:

- **Property purchase:** Requires property visits, which cannot be compressed into a single operational day. Most clients make a separate trip for property.
- **Moving household goods:** Shipping furniture, vehicles, or personal effects is a separate logistics process.

## When Two Trips Make Sense

For more complex cases, two trips spaced 3–4 months apart may be better:

Clients with families, multiple properties, or complex business structures often prefer this approach. It eliminates the pressure of a single high-stakes day.

## What Makes One Trip Work

- **Experienced local coordination.** Someone who has done this 50+ times, not someone learning on your dime.
- **Pre-booked appointments.** Walking in without an appointment is gambling. Pre-booked slots are the difference between a smooth day and a wasted one.
- **Document readiness.** Every document checked, every apostille verified, every translation completed before arrival.

posts.content:
## Your Dollar Goes 3x Further: The Head-to-Head Numbers

If you're an American considering a move abroad, the first question is always: how far does my dollar go? In Paraguay, the answer is roughly **three times further** than in most of the United States.

Let's break it down category by category.

## Overall Cost Comparison

| Category | Average US Cost | Average Paraguay Cost | Savings |
|----------|---------------|---------------------|---------|
| Rent (1BR, city center) | $1,800 | $450 | -75% |
| Rent (2BR, city center) | $2,500 | $650 | -74% |
| Rent (3BR, city center) | $3,500 | $900 | -74% |
| Groceries (monthly) | $500 | $225 | -55% |
| Healthcare (private insurance) | $500 | $75 | -85% |
| Utilities (monthly) | $200 | $110 | -45% |
| Dining out (restaurant meal) | $20 | $7 | -65% |
| Transportation (monthly) | $150 | $60 | -60% |
| Internet (monthly) | $70 | $35 | -50% |
| Gym membership | $50 | $30 | -40% |
| Domestic beer | $6 | $1.50 | -75% |
| Coffee (cafe) | $5 | $2 | -60% |
| **Total Monthly (comfortable)** | **$4,800** | **$1,450** | **-70%** |

## Detailed Breakdown

### Housing: 65-75% Cheaper

Housing is the biggest expense in the US and the biggest saving in Paraguay.

| Type | US City (Austin, TX) | Asuncion, PY | Difference |
|------|---------------------|-------------|-----------|
| Studio apartment | $1,200 | $350 | -71% |
| 1-bedroom (center) | $1,600 | $450 | -72% |
| 1-bedroom (outside center) | $1,200 | $350 | -71% |

| 2-bedroom (outside center) | $1,600 | $500 | -69% |
| 3-bedroom house | $2,800 | $900 | -68% |
| Luxury penthouse | $4,000 | $1,500 | -63% |

**What $1,500 gets you in each country:**

- **USA (any major city):** A one-bedroom apartment in a decent area, or a studio in a prime location
- **Paraguay:** A luxury 3-bedroom penthouse in the best neighborhood in Asuncion, with pool and security

### Food: 55% Cheaper

| Item | US Price | Paraguay Price | Savings |
|------|---------|---------------|---------|
| Weekly groceries (single) | $100 | $45 | -55% |
| Weekly groceries (family of 4) | $250 | $120 | -52% |
| Milk (1 gallon) | $4 | $2.50 | -38% |
| Eggs (dozen) | $4 | $1.50 | -63% |
| Chicken breast (1 lb) | $5 | $2 | -60% |
| Beef (1 lb) | $7 | $3 | -57% |

### Healthcare: 80-90% Cheaper

This is where the savings are most dramatic.

|---------|------------------------|------------------------|---------|
| GP visit | $150 | $25 | -83% |
| Specialist visit | $250 | $40 | -84% |
| Dentist cleaning | $150 | $30 | -80% |
| Emergency room visit | $2,000 | $100 | -95% |
| Hospital stay (per day) | $5,000 | $300 | -94% |
| Monthly health insurance (individual) | $500 | $75 | -85% |
| Monthly health insurance (couple) | $1,200 | $140 | -88% |
| Prescription (typical) | $50 | $12 | -76% |

**The math on healthcare alone:** A US couple paying $1,200/month for mediocre insurance can get excellent private coverage in Paraguay for $140/month — saving **$12,720/year**.

### Utilities: 45% Cheaper

| Utility | US Monthly Average | Paraguay Monthly Average | Savings |
|---------|-------------------|-------------------------|---------|
| Electricity | $120 | $60 | -50% |
| Water | $40 | $20 | -50% |
| Gas | $30 | $15 | -50% |
| Internet (100+ Mbps) | $70 | $35 | -50% |
| Phone plan (unlimited) | $50 | $15 | -70% |
| **Total** | **$310** | **$145** | **-53%** |

### Dining & Entertainment: 65% Cheaper

| Item | US Price | Paraguay Price | Savings |

| Inexpensive restaurant meal | $15 | $5 | -67% |
| Mid-range restaurant (3 courses) | $60 | $18 | -70% |

| Imported beer (pint) | $8 | $3 | -63% |

| Movie ticket | $14 | $5 | -64% |
| Cocktail bar (drink) | $15 | $6 | -60% |

### Transportation: 60% Cheaper

| Item | US Price | Paraguay Price | Savings |

| Bus ticket (one-way) | $2.50 | $0.35 | -86% |
| Monthly bus pass | $70 | $25 | -64% |
| Taxi (5 miles) | $15 | $5 | -67% |
| Uber/Bolt (5 miles) | $12 | $4 | -67% |
| Gasoline (gallon) | $3.50 | $5 | +43% |
| Car insurance (monthly) | $100 | $40 | -60% |

## The Lifestyle Multiplier Effect

This is the most important concept to understand.

Because Paraguay is so much cheaper across the board, your US dollars create a **lifestyle multiplier**. Here's what $3,000/month buys in each country:

| Category | US Budget | US Lifestyle | Paraguay Budget | Paraguay Lifestyle |
|----------|----------|-------------|----------------|-------------------|
| Housing | $1,500 | 1BR apartment, decent area | $650 | 3BR luxury penthouse |
| Food | $500 | Groceries + 4 takeout meals | $300 | Groceries + 12 restaurant meals |
| Healthcare | $500 | Basic insurance with high deductible | $140 | Premium international plan |
| Transport | $150 | Car payment portion or bus | $80 | Uber daily + occasional rental |
| Utilities | $200 | Standard | $110 | Fiber internet, full AC |
| Entertainment | $150 | 2-3 nights out | $200 | 8-10 nights out |
| **Total** | **$3,000** | **Middle-class, comfortable** | **$1,480** | **Upper-class luxury** |

**Result:** $3,000/month in the US = middle-class comfort with no frills. $3,000/month in Paraguay = elite lifestyle with high-end housing, frequent dining, premium healthcare, and $1,500/month left over for travel.

## What Different Budgets Buy

| Monthly Budget | US Lifestyle | Paraguay Lifestyle |
|---------------|-------------|-------------------|
| $1,000 | Roommate situation, basic food | Modest but independent, own 1BR |
| $1,500 | Studio, no car, limited social | Comfortable 2BR, dining out, social |
| $2,000 | 1BR, used car, tight budget | Premium 2BR, nice area, travel fund |
| $3,000 | Middle class, comfortable | Elite: luxury penthouse, top healthcare |
| $5,000 | Upper middle class, nice area | Luxury: house with pool, car, frequent travel |

## Hidden Savings in Paraguay

Beyond the obvious categories, Paraguay offers significant "hidden" savings:

### No Property Tax
Property taxes in Paraguay are negligible — typically $100-300/year on a $200K property. Compare to $4,000-8,000/year in most US states.

### No Capital Gains Tax
Sell investments, crypto, or property at a profit? 0% capital gains tax in Paraguay on foreign assets.

### Lower Utility Bills Year-Round
No heating bills needed (temperate winters) and moderate AC costs. Compare to US winter heating bills of $150-400/month.

### Cheaper Services
House cleaning: $10-15/visit. Personal training: $15-25/session. Massage: $20-30/hour. All 60-80% cheaper than the US.

## Where Paraguay Is More Expensive

It's honest to note where costs may be higher:

| Item | More Expensive? | Detail |
|------|---------------|--------|
| Gasoline | 40% more | $5/gallon vs $3.50 in US |
| Imported goods | 20-50% more | Electronics, luxury brands, some imports |
| International travel | Variable | Flights from Asuncion can be pricey |
| Car purchase | 30-50% more | Import duties on vehicles |
| Western-brand items | 20-40% more | Name-brand clothes, toiletries |

## The Bottom Line

The numbers are clear: **your US dollar goes 3x further in Paraguay.**

- Housing: 65-75% cheaper
- Food: 55% cheaper
- Healthcare: 70-85% cheaper
- Dining: 65% cheaper
- Transportation: 60% cheaper
- Utilities: 45% cheaper

A $3,000/month US budget becomes a $9,000-equivalent lifestyle in Paraguay. You don't just save money — you upgrade every aspect of your life.

**The same money that gives you a modest existence in the US buys you a luxury life in Paraguay.**

posts.title: US Social Security in Paraguay: Tax, Currency & Healthcare
posts.excerpt: US Social Security benefits are 100% tax-free in Paraguay thanks to its territorial tax system. Direct deposit works seamlessly, private healthcare costs $50-150/month, and there's no totalization agreement needed to keep receiving benefits.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
## Can You Collect US Social Security in Paraguay?

The short answer is yes. US citizens receiving Social Security can happily collect their benefits while living in Paraguay. Here's everything you need to know.

## Tax: The Best Part

### Social Security in Paraguay: 0% Tax

Paraguay's territorial tax system taxes only income generated within Paraguay. US Social Security benefits are foreign-source income, and **Paraguay does not tax foreign income**.

This means your Social Security payments arrive in your Paraguayan bank account entirely tax-free at the local level.

### What About US Tax?

The US taxes Social Security benefits based on your combined income. As a US citizen living abroad:

- You still file US tax returns (US citizens are taxed on worldwide income regardless of residence)
- Social Security benefits may be subject to US federal tax if your combined income exceeds certain thresholds ($25K individual, $32K joint)
- The Foreign Earned Income Exclusion (FEIE) does **not** apply to Social Security income (it's unearned income)
- However, the **Foreign Tax Credit** can offset any US tax if you pay foreign tax — but since you pay 0% in Paraguay, this doesn't help directly
- Most retirees with Social Security as their primary income fall below the taxable thresholds anyway

| Annual Social Security Income | Taxable in US? | Taxable in Paraguay? | Effective Rate |
|------------------------------|----------------|---------------------|---------------|
| $12,000 (average benefit) | No (below threshold) | 0% | 0% |
| $20,000 | No (below threshold) | 0% | 0% |
| $30,000 | Up to 50% taxable (about $1,500) | 0% | ~5% US only |
| $45,000 (max benefit) | Up to 85% taxable (about $6,500) | 0% | ~14% US only |

**Important:** Even if some US tax applies, it's far less than what you'd pay living in most countries. And if your savings are modest, you'll likely owe $0 in US tax on your Social Security.

## Direct Deposit: Does It Work?

Yes. US Social Security benefits are paid to beneficiaries regardless of where they live (with very few exceptions for certain countries). Paraguay is fully supported.

### Setting Up Direct Deposit to Paraguay

1. **Open a Paraguayan bank account** — This is straightforward with residency. Major banks include:
   - Banco Itau
   - Banco Continental
   - Banco Regional
   - Ueno Bank (digital-friendly)

2. **Update your SSA direct deposit info** — Log into your My Social Security account or call the Federal Benefits Unit in Buenos Aires

3. **Provide your Paraguayan bank details** — You'll need:
   - Bank name and address in Paraguay
   - Account number
   - SWIFT/IBAN code

4. **Confirm receipt** — Transfers typically arrive in 1-3 business days

### Alternative: US Bank Account + ATM

Many retirees prefer to keep a US bank account and use Paraguayan ATMs. Paraguay has extensive ATM networks, and withdrawal fees are minimal (typically $1-3 per transaction).

## US-Paraguay Totalization Agreement

There is **no totalization agreement** between the US and Paraguay. A totalization agreement coordinates Social Security coverage between two countries to avoid double taxation and fill gaps in work history.

**What this means for you:**

- If you worked 10+ years in the US (40 quarters), you're fully vested and receive full benefits regardless of where you live
- If you split your career between the US and Paraguay without reaching 40 quarters in the US, you may not qualify for US Social Security benefits at all
- Paraguay doesn't have its own social security system that covers US expats, so there's no coordination needed
- **For most US retirees who worked most of their career in the US, the lack of a totalization agreement doesn't matter**

## Healthcare in Paraguay

One of the biggest concerns for US retirees on Social Security is healthcare. Paraguay offers an affordable private healthcare system that works well for retirees.

### Private Health Insurance Costs

| Plan Type | Monthly Premium (Individual) | Coverage |
|-----------|---------------------------|----------|
| Basic local plan | $35-50 | GP visits, basic hospitalization |
| Standard local plan | $50-80 | Specialist visits, hospitalization, some procedures |
| Premium local plan | $80-120 | Full coverage, private rooms, dental |
| International plan | $100-150 | Global coverage incl. USA |

### Top Private Hospitals in Asuncion

| Hospital | Quality Rating | English-Speaking Staff | Typical Services |
|----------|---------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| Hospital Privado Franco | Excellent | Yes | Full-service, specialists |
| Sanatorio Migone | Excellent | Yes | Full-service, maternity |
| Hospital de Clinicas | Good | Limited | Teaching hospital, lower cost |
| Sanatorio Britanico | Very Good | Yes | International patients |

### Healthcare Quality

- Private healthcare in Paraguay is **comparable to US community hospitals**
- Doctors often trained in US or Europe
- English widely spoken in private hospitals
- Wait times are **significantly shorter** than the US or UK
- Out-of-pocket costs are **80-90% less** than US prices

### Medicare in Paraguay

Medicare does **not** cover healthcare outside the US. You cannot use Medicare benefits in Paraguay. However:

- You can keep Medicare Part A (free, hospital insurance) for if you visit the US
- You can drop Medicare Part B (saves $174.70/month) since you can't use it abroad
- You may want to keep Part A as a safety net for US visits

## Cost of Living on Social Security

The average US Social Security benefit in 2026 is approximately $1,900/month. In Paraguay, this provides:

| Monthly Budget Item | Average Cost in PY | What You Get |
|--------------------|-------------------|-------------|
| Rent (1BR modern) | $400-500 | Villa Morra/Carmelitas |
| Groceries | $200-300 | Fresh produce, meat, imports |
| Utilities | $60-100 | Electric, water, gas |
| Internet | $25-40 | 100-200 Mbps fiber |
| Health insurance | $50-80 | Private plan |
| Dining out | $150-250 | 8-12 restaurant meals |
| Transportation | $40-60 | Uber/Bolt |
| Entertainment | $100-150 | Activities, hobbies |
| **Total** | **$1,025-1,480** | **Comfortable lifestyle** |

**Result:** A retiree on average Social Security ($1,900/mo) lives **comfortably** in Paraguay with money left over for travel.

## Comparison: Social Security Income in Other Countries

| Destination | Tax on SS | Cost of Living (Comfortable) | SS $1,900/mo Enough? | Healthcare Cost |
|------------|----------|-----------------------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| **Paraguay** | 0% | $1,100-1,500/mo | Yes | $50-80/mo |
| Costa Rica | 0% | $2,000-3,000/mo | Tight | $80-150/mo |
| Panama | 0% | $1,800-2,500/mo | Tight | $80-150/mo |
| Mexico | 0-30% | $1,500-2,500/mo | Tight | $50-100/mo |
| Thailand | 0-35% | $1,200-2,000/mo | Yes (tight) | $50-80/mo |
| Portugal | 10-28% | $2,000-3,000/mo | No | $50-100/mo |

## Real Example

**Mike and Susan, retired couple from Florida:**

- Combined Social Security: $3,400/month
- Paraguay monthly expenses: $1,850
- Savings: $1,550/month
- Tax in Paraguay on SS: $0
- Tax in US: $0 (below combined income threshold)

**Annual savings vs living in the US:** $28,000+

## The Bottom Line

US Social Security in Paraguay is a powerful combination:

- **0% tax** on benefits
- **Seamless direct deposit** to Paraguayan banks
- **Affordable healthcare** — $50-150/month for excellent private coverage
- **$1,900/month SS benefit** funds a comfortable lifestyle
- **No totalization agreement needed** if you have 40+ US work quarters

**Your Social Security dollar goes 2-3x further in Paraguay.**
